definition_zh: 扭打；搏斗；努力应付；竭力解决； grapple with 设法对付
definition_en: to fight or struggle with someone or something, especially by holding on tightly, or to try hard to deal with a difficult problem
core_image: 两手死死扣住对方，在泥地里扭成一团，谁也不肯松手
scene: 谈判拖到深夜，几位代表围着边境和渔民的问题吵得面红耳赤，却始终没能拿出方案。All night the delegates grappled with the question of the border without reaching any agreement.
sceneCN: 这里 grapple 是「努力对付（难题）」（第 2 个义项：竭力处理棘手的事）；句意：整夜代表们都在设法解决边境问题，却没能达成协议。

pos.zh: 扭打；搏斗；努力应付；设法解决
扭打；搏斗；（抓钩形的）抓斗

collocations.zh: 与过去纠缠、艰难面对既往

derivatives.zh: 扭斗术；擒抱（由 grapple 加 -ing 构成的动名词，后来成为摔跤技术的名称）
扭打着；擒抱型摔跤手（由 grapple 加 -er 表示从事该动作的人）
四爪锚；抓钩（与 grapple 同源，同出古法语「抓钩」一词，但拼写已分道）

senses.title: To seize and wrestle with
senses.definition: to seize someone or something firmly and struggle with them by closing in and holding tight
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住某人或某物，贴身缠住并用力扭打
senses.example: Two sailors grappled on the wet deck.
senses.exampleCN: 两名水手在湿漉漉的甲板上扭打起来。
senses.why: The word first named an iron hook that grips, so to grapple meant to close on and grip in a fight.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指会死死咬住的铁钩，所以动词本义就是贴身缠斗、以抓住为要点。

senses.title: To struggle with a hard problem
senses.definition: to try hard to deal with or make sense of a difficult subject or situation
senses.definitionCN: 下大力气去处理或理解一个困难的问题、局面
senses.example: Cities are grappling with a shortage of affordable housing.
senses.exampleCN: 各城市都在努力应对经济适用住房的短缺。
senses.why: A stubborn difficulty is pictured as a strong opponent that must be gripped and wrestled before it yields.
senses.whyCN: 难缠的问题被想成一名强壮的对手，只有先抓住并扭打，它才会被制服。

senses.title: To grip firmly with the hands
senses.definition: to hold on to something tightly, especially in a struggle to gain a grip or pull oneself along
senses.definitionCN: 用手紧紧抓住某物，多指在努力抓住或攀拉时的动作
senses.example: He grappled for a hold on the smooth rock face.
senses.exampleCN: 他在光滑的岩壁上摸索着想抓住点什么。
senses.why: Long before it described fighting, the same root meant a small hook, so grabbing a firm hold is the simplest act behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 在同源词义中，这个词根早先就指小钩子，因此「抓牢一个把手」正是这一词义最简单的动作来源。

senses.title: To come to grips with
senses.definition: to engage seriously with a challenge or responsibility instead of avoiding it
senses.definitionCN: 认真投入地面对挑战或责任，而不是回避
senses.example: The council finally grappled with the port expansion plan.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会终于开始认真处理港口扩建方案。
senses.why: From fighting physically, the verb came to mean taking hold of a matter and refusing to let it go until it is settled.
senses.whyCN: 从身体上的搏斗出发，动词引申为抓住一件事不放，直到把它办妥为止。

senses.title: A close physical fight
senses.definition: a rough fight at close quarters in which the opponents seize and hold each other
senses.definitionCN: 近距离的粗暴争斗，双方互相擒抱、扭缠
senses.example: The police broke up a grapple outside the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 警察制止了体育场外的一场扭打。
senses.why: The noun keeps the original picture of a scrap fought with hands and arms, not with words.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了最初那幅用拳脚缠斗而非靠口头争执的画面。

senses.title: A hook-like gripping tool
senses.definition: a tool or device with bent prongs used for seizing and lifting heavy objects
senses.definitionCN: 带弯爪、用来抓住并吊起重物的工具或装置
senses.example: A grapple was lowered to lift the sunken logs.
senses.exampleCN: 人们放下一个抓钩去吊起沉在水底的圆木。
senses.why: The oldest name for the word was the hook itself, and that tool sense survives in logging and salvage work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的说法就是那枚铁钩本身，这一工具义至今仍留在伐木与打捞作业中。

intro.en: Grapple comes from Old French grappil, a hook, from grappe meaning a bunch of grapes, perhaps from the idea of bent claws or tendrils.
intro.cn: grapple 来自古法语 grappil（钩子），源头是 grappe（一串葡萄），可能取葡萄弯爪般的卷须之形。

items.en: A reconstructed form krampon is generally thought to underlie the Germanic hook words.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 krampon 是日耳曼语中一批「钩子」词的共同来源。

items.en: A Germanic hook word passes into French and gives grappe, a cluster of grapes.
items.cn: 一个日耳曼语「钩子」词传入法语，形成 grappe，意为「一串葡萄」。

items.en: Grappil names a hook or grapnel, and the verb grapiller means to seize.
items.cn: grappil 指钩子或小抓锚，动词 grapiller 意为抓取。

items.en: Grapple appears as a ship name for a grappling iron.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语出现表示「抓船钩」的 grapple。

items.en: The noun extends to a close fight and the verb to wrestling.
items.cn: 名词扩展出「近身搏斗」义，动词则用于扭打。

items.en: The phrase grapple with broadens the word to problems and ideas.
items.cn: 搭配 grapple with 把词义扩展到抽象的问题与观念。

note.en: Grapple is a hook that closes on its object, and the word now covers both rough fighting and hard thinking.
note.cn: grapple 是一枚会咬住东西的钩子，如今既指粗暴搏斗，也指苦苦思索。

entries.definition: a small anchor with several curved claws
entries.definitionCN: 多爪小锚；四爪锚（与 grapple 同出古法语「抓钩」一词，同样带勾抓之意）

entries.definition: a person who wrestles at close quarters
entries.definitionCN: 扭打者；擒抱型摔跤手（由 grapple 加表人后缀 -er 构成）

entries.definition: a style of wrestling with close holds, or the act of struggling
entries.definitionCN: 擒抱摔跤；扭斗（grapple 的动名词形式，也成为一个摔跤项目名）

entries.definition: to fight by holding and trying to throw an opponent down
entries.definitionCN: 扭打；摔跤（强调想把对方摔倒，grapple 更侧重死死抓住不放）

entries.definition: to make a determined effort to deal with a problem
entries.definitionCN: 着手处理；应付（多用于中性或积极的语境，缺少 grapple 那种吃力感）

entries.definition: to struggle against a difficulty or rival
entries.definitionCN: 争斗；应付（倾向于强调对抗与较量，与 grapple 的抓握意象不同）

normalIntro.en: Grapple is a hook from the start: French grappil was an iron claw, and the fighting sense grew out of gripping.
normalIntro.cn: grapple 从出生起就是一只钩子：古法语 grappil 指铁爪，搏斗义正是从「死死抓住」长出来的。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is grapple with, not grapple at.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 grapple with，而不是 grapple at。

normal.en: Grapple with a problem is the most common use in exams.
normal.cn: 应试中最常见的用法是 grapple with a problem（努力解决难题）。

normal.en: The same -ple ending appears in grapple, grapnel, and grappling.
normal.cn: 同样的 -ple 词尾出现在 grapple、grapnel、grappling 这一组词里。

normal.en: Grapple and grasp share the grabbing idea, but grapple adds struggle.
normal.cn: grapple 与 grasp 都含「抓」的意思，但 grapple 多了一层挣扎与较劲。

normal.en: In wrestling, a grappler closes in and holds on; so does the mind on a hard question.
normal.cn: 摔跤中 grappler 要贴身抱住对手，头脑处理难题时也正是这样缠着不放。

abstract.en: Picture two men locked arm to arm, mud under their boots.
abstract.cn: 想象两个男人手臂绞在一起，靴子陷在泥里。

abstract.en: Imagine a scholar gripping a knotted rope and pulling knot by knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学者抓住一根打满结的绳子，一个结一个结地往外拉。

abstract.en: See an iron hook biting into a log and being hauled up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只铁钩咬住圆木，被一点点往上拽。

examples.en: Researchers are still grappling with the cause of the disease.
examples.cn: 研究人员仍在竭力弄清这种病的成因。

examples.en: The two boys grappled in the snow until their coats were soaked.
examples.cn: 两个男孩在雪地里扭打，直到大衣全湿透了。

examples.en: It is a question that every generation must grapple with.
examples.cn: 这是一个每一代人都必须努力应对的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓住扑了」——扑上去一把抓住，就是扭打搏斗；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为，重构的日耳曼语形式 krampon（钩、爪）经法兰克语进入法语，形成 grappe（一串葡萄）；古法语 grappil 指钩子、抓锚，动词 grapiller 意为抓取，后进入英语成为 grapple：先指铁钩与抓钩，再由「抓住」发展为「扭打」「抓牢」「努力应付」。词根存疑之处在于日耳曼语源只有重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Grapple is the act of a hook that grips: a close fight comes first, then gripping with the hands, then grappling with problems, and the noun keeps both the fight and the tool.
sensesIntro.cn: grapple 就是「钩子咬住东西」这一动作：先有近身扭打，再是徒手抓牢，再引申为对付难题；名词则保留了搏斗与工具两种义，即抓钩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands locked on an opponent and refusing to let go.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手死死扣住对手，谁也不松。

branches.en: A close struggle is the earliest verbal sense.
branches.cn: 近身扭打是最早动词义项。

branches.en: Dealing with problems borrows the wrestling image.
branches.cn: 对付难题借用了摔跤的意象。

branches.en: Gripping with the hands is the literal act.
branches.cn: 用手抓牢是字面动作。

branches.en: The noun keeps the close fight as a thing.
branches.cn: 名词把近身扭打凝固成一件事。

branches.en: The hook is the oldest object behind the word.
branches.cn: 抓钩是这个词背后最古老的实物。

intro.en: Grapple has no productive prefix; its family is built with the endings -ing, -er, and the related noun grapnel.
intro.cn: grapple 没有能产的词缀，它的词族靠后缀 -ing、-er 以及与它同源的 grapnel 构成。

latinIntro.en: No secure Latin ancestor is attested, because this word reaches English through French from a Germanic form; grapnel is its closest relative.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经法语来自日耳曼语形，没有可靠的拉丁语祖形；最亲近的同源词是 grapnel。

items.example: Old French grappil gives the English word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 grappil 是英语这个词的来源。

items.example: Grappe carries the hooked-cluster image.
items.exampleCN: grappe 带着「一簇钩状物」的联想。

items.meaning: to fight closely or struggle with a problem
items.example: The verb is the everyday core form.
items.exampleCN: 动词形式是这个词最日常的核心。

items.meaning: a close fight or a gripping iron
items.example: The noun names both the fight and the tool.
items.exampleCN: 名词既指搏斗也指工具。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms grappling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 grappling。

items.example: Grappling names a close-hold sport.
items.exampleCN: grappling 是一门擒抱类运动的名字。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作执行者的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms grappler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 grappler。

items.meaning: a wrestler who fights at close quarters
items.example: A grappler relies on holds, not strikes.
items.exampleCN: 擒抱型选手靠抓抱而不靠打击。

items.example: Grapnel shares the hooked shape but not the spelling.
items.exampleCN: grapnel 共享钩形意象，拼写却不同。

definition_zh: 蚱蜢；蝗虫；跳跃高手；儿童游戏名
definition_en: a jumping insect with long hind legs that feeds on grass and leaves, or someone who hops about with quick nervous movements
core_image: 一只细长的绿虫伏在草叶上，两条长后腿一蹬，整个身子弹向半空
scene: 夏天的午后，草丛忽然安静，一个绿色的小东西突然蹦过石阶，又钻进草里不见了。A tiny green grasshopper jumped across the sunlit path and vanished into the grass.
sceneCN: 这里 grasshopper 是「蚱蜢」（第 1 个义项：以草叶为食、靠长后腿跳跃的昆虫）；句意：一只小小的绿蚱蜢跳过洒满阳光的小路，又消失在草丛里。

pos.zh: 蚱蜢；蝗虫；跳跃高手；儿童游戏名

derivatives.zh: 草（grasshopper 的前半部分，直接点明这种昆虫的活动场所与食物）
跳跃者；漏斗（由动词 hop 加 -er 构成，是 grasshopper 的后半部分）
蝗莺（一种鸣声似蚱蜢擦翅的鸟，由 grasshopper 与 warbler 组合而成）

senses.title: The leaping green insect
senses.definition: a slender plant-eating insect with strong hind legs on which it springs through grass
senses.definitionCN: 一种细长的食草昆虫，后腿发达，能弹跳着穿行草丛
senses.example: A grasshopper landed on my sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚱蜢落到我的袖子上。
senses.why: The name simply joins two facts about the creature: it lives in grass and it hops.
senses.whyCN: 这个词名把这种虫子的两件事直接拼在一起：生活在草里，靠蹦跳前进。

senses.title: Someone who hops about
senses.titleCN: 蹦蹦跳跳的人；坐不住的人
senses.definition: a person who moves with quick, restless hops, often applied to a lively or fidgety child
senses.definitionCN: 动作急促、不安分地蹦来蹦去的人，常用来形容活泼或坐不住的孩子
senses.example: The little grasshopper would not sit still for the photo.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小家伙一刻也不肯坐定，照片总拍不好。
senses.why: The same image of springing from place to place is transferred from the insect to an active person.
senses.whyCN: 「从一处弹到另一处」的画面被从昆虫身上移到活泼好动的人身上。

senses.title: A type of hopping game
senses.definition: a hopping game played by children in which players hop on one foot and must be neatly caught or jumped over, also called hunter and grasshopper
senses.definitionCN: 一种儿童游戏，玩家单脚跳，被抓住或被要求跳过时须干净利落，又称猎人与蚱蜢
senses.example: The children played grasshopper on the pavement.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在人行道上玩跳房子游戏。
senses.why: The game took its name from the creature because it is played with exactly that kind of hopping.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏正因为玩起来就是蚱蜢式的一跳一跳，才借用了它的名字。

senses.title: A nickname for a jumper
senses.titleCN: 跳跃好手；弹跳力强的人
senses.definition: a joking or admiring name for someone who jumps unusually well or unusually high
senses.definitionCN: 对弹跳力出众或跳得特别高的人的戏称或赞称
senses.example: The coach calls the new forward a grasshopper for his jumps.
senses.exampleCN: 教练因为新前锋弹跳好，管他叫「蚱蜢」。
senses.why: The insect is famous only for its leap, so the name naturally became a compliment about jumping.
senses.whyCN: 蚱蜢最出名的本事就是跳跃，所以这个名字很自然地变成了对弹跳的夸奖。

senses.title: A mixed drink
senses.definition: a sweet after-dinner drink made from green mint liqueur, white cacao, and cream
senses.definitionCN: 一种餐后甜酒，用绿色薄荷利口酒、白可可酒和奶油调成
senses.example: The barman shook a grasshopper for our dessert.
senses.exampleCN: 调酒师为我们的餐后甜点摇了一杯蚱蜢鸡尾酒。
senses.why: The pale green colour of the drink recalls the insect, and the name is pure appearance.
senses.whyCN: 这种酒淡淡的绿色让人想到这种昆虫，名字纯粹取的是颜色相像。

intro.en: Grasshopper is a transparent English compound: grass plus hop, with the agent ending -er, so it means the thing that hops in the grass.
intro.cn: grasshopper 是清晰的英语复合词：grass（草）加 hop（跳），再加表示「做某事的东西」的 -er，意为「在草里跳的东西」。

items.en: Greashoppa is recorded as a name for the insect, built from grass and hopper.
items.cn: 古英语 greashoppa 已用来称这种昆虫，由 grass 与 hopper 组成。

items.en: The spelling settles towards grasshopper as grass took its modern form.
items.cn: 随着 grass 定形为现代拼写，词形逐渐稳定为 grasshopper。

items.en: The word begins to be used playfully of hopping people.
items.cn: 这个词开始被戏谑地用来指蹦跳的人。

items.en: Grasshopper names a hopping game played by children in Victorian schoolyards.
items.cn: 十九世纪英国学校的操场上，grasshopper 成为一种跳跃游戏的名字。

items.en: The green cocktail adds a very different, purely visual sense.
items.cn: 绿色鸡尾酒又添了一个纯靠颜色联想的新义。

note.en: Grasshopper is a literal grass-and-hop compound, easily confused with cousins among insects and with words that only borrow its hopping picture.
note.cn: grasshopper 是「草 + 跳」的字面复合词，容易与昆虫亲戚以及只是借用其跳跃意象的词混淆。

entries.definition: the low green plants that cover fields
entries.definitionCN: 草（grasshopper 的前半部分，说明它栖身何处、吃些什么）

entries.definition: something or someone that hops
entries.definitionCN: 跳跃的东西（grasshopper 的后半部分，点明它的看家本领）

entries.definition: a small brown songbird with an insect-like rattle
entries.definitionCN: 蝗莺（一种小型棕色鸣禽，鸣声像蚱蜢擦翅，名字由 grasshopper 与 warbler 合成）

entries.definition: a large grasshopper that migrates and strips crops in swarms
entries.definitionCN: 蝗虫（与蚱蜢同类，但成群迁飞啃食庄稼，因此指近义却略带灾祸感）

entries.definition: a dark brown insect that sings at night
entries.definitionCN: 蟋蟀（同为直翅目昆虫，但多在夜间鸣叫，不常大群迁飞）

entries.definition: an American long-horned insect that rubs its wings to make sound
entries.definitionCN: 蝈蝈儿；螽斯（北美常见的长角型昆虫，以擦翅鸣叫闻名）

normalIntro.en: Grasshopper is one of the easiest words to build: put grass and hop together and the insect appears.
normalIntro.cn: grasshopper 是最容易拆解的单词之一：把 grass 与 hop 放在一起，这只虫子就出现了。

normal.en: Grass tells you where it lives; hop tells you how it moves.
normal.cn: grass 告诉你在哪住，hop 告诉你怎么走。

normal.en: Keep the -er ending, since it is the thing that hops.
normal.cn: 别忘了 -er 词尾，因为它是「会跳的东西」。

normal.en: The plural is grasshoppers, and the word does not take a rare form.
normal.cn: 复数是 grasshoppers，这个词没有少见的变化形式。

normal.en: Compare locust: a grasshopper is the insect, a locust is one that swarms.
normal.cn: 对比 locust：grasshopper 是这种昆虫的通称，locust 专指成群成灾的那一类。

normal.en: The drink called a grasshopper is green, which shows how the name travels by colour.
normal.cn: 叫 grasshopper 的鸡尾酒是绿色的，可见这个名字也会靠颜色流传。

abstract.en: Picture a green spring loaded under a blade of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一根草叶下压着一只绿色的弹簧。

abstract.en: Imagine a child hopping between chalk squares on a pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子在人行道的粉笔格子间单脚跳。

abstract.en: Think of a coin-flat glass of pale green drink on a white cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象白桌布上放着一只浅绿色的扁酒杯。

examples.en: The field was loud with grasshoppers in the late summer.
examples.cn: 夏末的田野里满是蚱蜢的鸣声。

examples.en: In dry years, grasshoppers can strip an entire meadow.
examples.cn: 在干旱的年份，蚱蜢能把整片草地啃光。

examples.en: She ordered a grasshopper after dinner.
examples.cn: 她餐后点了一杯蚱蜢鸡尾酒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「草扑」——草里扑腾一下跳出来的虫，就是蚱蜢；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 greashoppa 由 grass（草）与 hopper（跳跃者，hop 加 -er）合成，中古英语时期随 grass 的拼写定形而成为 grasshopper；字面即「草里跳跃的东西」。这是地道的英语复合构词，没有拉丁语或希腊语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the insect, then lends its hopping motion to people and games, and its green colour to a cocktail.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先从昆虫说起，接着把「一蹦一跳」的动作借给人和游戏，最后又把它的绿色借给了一杯鸡尾酒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green insect springing out of the grass on long back legs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只绿色昆虫用长长的后腿从草丛里蹦出来。

branches.en: The insect is the literal sense and the base of everything else.
branches.cn: 昆虫是字面义项，也是其余义项的根基。

branches.en: People take over the insect praise of hopping.
branches.cn: 人以昆虫「能跳」这一长处自比。

branches.en: The game borrows the same hopping action.
branches.cn: 游戏借用了同一套蹦跳动作。

branches.en: A green drink borrows only the colour.
branches.cn: 绿色的酒只借走了颜色。

branches.en: Insect and cocktail share nothing but pale green.
branches.cn: 昆虫与鸡尾酒除了浅绿之外毫无共同之处。

intro.en: Grasshopper is a compound of two free stems plus the agent suffix -er, which is why it is spelled as one word.
intro.cn: grasshopper 由两个自由词干再加表施事的后缀 -er 合成，所以拼成一个词。

latinIntro.en: Genuine insect names in Latin, such as locusta and gryllus, are unrelated to grasshopper, so there is no Latin relative to list.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语里真正的昆虫名如 locusta、gryllus 与 grasshopper 无亲缘关系，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.example: Grass supplies the habitat in the name.
items.exampleCN: grass 在词里提供了栖息地。

items.meaning: to move with quick small jumps
items.example: Hop supplies the action in the name.
items.exampleCN: hop 在词里提供了动作。

items.example: The suffix -er turns hop into hopper.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 hop 变成 hopper。

items.meaning: a hopping creature or a funnel
items.example: Hopper names whatever hops.
items.exampleCN: hopper 指会跳跃的东西。

items.example: The compound keeps the two stems whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把两个词干完整保留下来。

items.example: The plural only adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数只加 -s。

items.meaning: a bird that sounds like the insect
items.example: The bird name reuses the insect name.
items.exampleCN: 这种鸟的名字直接复用了昆虫名。

items.meaning: of the colour of fresh grass
items.example: Grass-green shares the grass stem.
items.exampleCN: grass-green 共享 grass 这一词干。

items.example: Hopping is the root verb at work.
items.exampleCN: hopping 体现出核心动词 hop。

definition_zh: 长满草的；多草的；草绿色的；草味的
definition_en: covered with grass or full of grass, or having the colour or smell of fresh grass
core_image: 一片缓坡从脚下铺开，绿草密密盖住泥土，风一吹整坡都在轻轻晃动
scene: 风从山坡那边吹过来，孩子们在缓坡上打滚，衣服上蹭满了青草，一股清香一直跟到回家。They rolled down the grassy slope until their clothes smelled of green blades.
sceneCN: 这里 grassy 是「长满草的」（第 1 个义项：地面被草覆盖）；句意：他们沿着长满草的山坡滚下来，直到衣服都沾满青草的气味。

pos.zh: 长满草的；多草的；草绿色的；草味的

derivatives.zh: 草（grassy 的基础名词，加 -y 后表示「长满草的」）
看上去像草地的（grassy 与 looking 组合成的临时复合形容词）
多草；草色（grassy 去掉 y 加 -ness 构成的名词，表示「多草的性质」）

senses.title: Covered with grass
senses.definition: having the ground covered with grass, either planted or growing wild
senses.definitionCN: 地面被草覆盖，无论是人工栽种还是自然生长
senses.example: Cattle grazed quietly on the grassy slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 牛群在长满草的坡地上安静地吃草。
senses.why: The ending -y works like English -y elsewhere: it says that the thing is full of what the noun names, so grassy means full of grass.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 在英语里常表示「充满名词所指之物」，所以 grassy 就是「长满草的」。

senses.title: Of the colour of grass
senses.definition: of a fresh green colour like that of summer grass
senses.definitionCN: 像盛夏青草那样的鲜绿色
senses.example: She painted the walls a grassy green.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了一种草绿色。
senses.why: Because grass is the most ordinary green in a landscape, the colour took over the adjective by extension.
senses.whyCN: 草是风景里最常见的绿色，于是这个形容词顺势把「绿」也收进了词义。

senses.title: Smelling or tasting of grass
senses.definition: having a fresh smell or taste that recalls cut or crushed grass
senses.definitionCN: 带有新鲜青草那种气味或味道的
senses.example: The wine is light and pleasantly grassy.
senses.exampleCN: 这款酒清淡爽口，带一点青草香。
senses.why: The same -y pattern that names a colour also names a smell, as with honey and honeyed perfume.
senses.whyCN: 与表示颜色同样的 -y 构词方式也用来表示气味，类似用名词描写某种气味的做法。

senses.title: Inland and green
senses.titleCN: 绿草葱茏的（多用于地名）
senses.definition: descriptive of land that is green with grass rather than bare, sand, or rock
senses.definitionCN: 形容土地因草而绿，而不是光秃、沙地或裸岩
senses.example: We walked up from the beach onto the grassy plain.
senses.exampleCN: 我们从海滩走上绿草覆盖的平原。
senses.why: Geographers and writers keep the plain descriptive force of the word to contrast green land with barren land.
senses.whyCN: 地理描述与文学写作保留了这个词朴素的描写力，用它来对比绿草之地与荒芜之地。

senses.title: Crude as a joke name for cannabis
senses.titleCN: 形容大麻的俚俗用法（多作漫画名）
senses.definition: applied loosely and informally to strong-smelling cannabis, as a jokey description rather than a standard label
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地用来形容气味浓烈的大麻，只是戏谑描写，并非标准术语
senses.example: In the comic strip the plant was simply called grassy.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部连环画里，那种植物只被叫作「草味的」。
senses.why: Since cannabis is often called grass, the adjective follows the noun into slang use.
senses.whyCN: 因为大麻在俚语里常被叫作 grass，这个形容词也跟着名词一起进入了俚语用法。

intro.en: Grassy is a native English adjective built from grass with the adjectival ending -y, meaning full of or like grass.
intro.cn: grassy 是地道的英语形容词，由 grass 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，意为「充满草或像草的」。

items.en: Græs names the green ground plant that cattle eat.
items.cn: 古英语 græs 指牛吃的绿色地面植物，即草。

items.en: Adjectives in -ig were already formed on nouns, giving the pattern for grassy.
items.cn: 古英语早已用 -ig 后缀加在名词上造形容词，为 grassy 提供了构词模式。

items.en: Grassy appears as an adjective meaning covered with grass.
items.cn: 中古英语中 grassy 作为「长满草的」形容词出现。

items.en: The word extends to the colour and smell of fresh grass.
items.cn: 十六世纪前后，这个词扩展到表示青草的颜色与气味。

items.en: Grassy crops up in place names, wine notes, and comic slang.
items.cn: 现代英语中，grassy 出现在地名、品酒词与漫画俚语里。

note.en: Grassy is the colour-free sibling of grass words, related to the noun grass and to the ending -y that marks fullness.
note.cn: grassy 是草类词里不带具体色彩的形容词，与名词 grass 以及表「充满」的后缀 -y 相关。

entries.definition: the low green plants that cover the ground
entries.definitionCN: 草（grassy 的基础名词，去掉形容词后缀即它是本体）

entries.definition: the quality of being full of grass
entries.definitionCN: 多草；草色（grassy 加 -ness 得来的名词）

entries.definition: a colour name made by adding green to grassy
entries.definitionCN: 草绿色（在 grassy 后面加 green 构成的颜色名称）

entries.definition: green with growing plants
entries.definitionCN: 草木葱茏的（较书面，多用于形容风景，比 grassy 更文雅）

entries.definition: an area covered with mown grass
entries.definitionCN: 草坪；修剪过的草地（是修剪整齐的草地面，grassy 只是说「有草」）

entries.definition: a field of grass and wildflowers left for hay
entries.definitionCN: 草甸；牧草地（野花与草混杂的田野，规模与用途都比 grassy 更具体）

normalIntro.en: Grassy is grass plus -y, the same pattern that turns salt into salty and cloud into cloudy.
normalIntro.cn: grassy 就是 grass 加 -y，与 salt 变 salty、cloud 变 cloudy 是同一套构词方式。

normal.en: The suffix -y in grassy means full of, so grassy means full of grass.
normal.cn: grassy 里的 -y 表示「充满」，所以 grassy 就是「长满草」。

normal.en: Drop the final -s and add -y: grass becomes grassy.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：去掉 grass 末尾的 -s，再加 -y，得到 grassy。

normal.en: The comparative is grassier and the superlative is grassiest.
normal.cn: 比较级是 grassier，最高级是 grassiest。

normal.en: Grassy slope, grassy field, and grassy bank are the most common pairings.
normal.cn: 最常见的搭配是 grassy slope、grassy field 与 grassy bank。

normal.en: Grassy is adjective only, so a patch of grass is still called grass, not grassy.
normal.cn: grassy 只作形容词，称呼一片草时仍用名词 grass，不说 grassy。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket of green ticking in the wind over bare earth.
abstract.cn: 想象裸露的泥土上盖着一层随风轻抖的绿毯。

abstract.en: Think of a crayon called grassy green half-used in a child box.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子的蜡笔盒里有一支用了一半的「草绿」。

abstract.en: Smell the sharp sweetness of grass crushed under a wheel.
abstract.cn: 闻一闻车轮碾过青草时那股尖锐的清香。

examples.en: They set up their tent on a grassy patch beside the stream.
examples.cn: 他们在溪边长草的一小块地上搭起了帐篷。

examples.en: The lawn had turned grassy again after the spring rain.
examples.cn: 春雨过后，那块草坪又长满了草。

examples.en: The tea had a grassy flavour that some people love.
examples.cn: 这茶带一种青草味，有人非常喜欢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格雷西」——叫格雷西的姑娘喜欢躺在草地上，草地就是 grassy；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: grassy 是英语原生形容词：名词 grass（古英语 græs，草）加形容词后缀 -y（-ig 的现代形式，表示「充满、具有……性质」），即「长满草的」，与 salty、cloudy 同类；词源上没有拉丁语或希腊语祖形。

sensesIntro.en: Grassy begins with the ground itself being covered by grass, then lends the noun colour and smell, and finally drifts into descriptive and slang uses.
sensesIntro.cn: grassy 先指地面被草覆盖，再把「草」的颜色与气味借过来，最后进入描写性用法与俚俗用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slope where green blades hide every bit of soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：整坡绿草把泥土完全遮住的坡地。

branches.en: Both covered ground and inland landscape rest on the first image.
branches.cn: 「被草覆盖」与「绿草之地」都建立在第一个意象上。

branches.en: Colour is borrowed from the noun grass.
branches.cn: 颜色义是从名词 grass 借来的。

branches.en: Smell is borrowed in exactly the same way as colour.
branches.cn: 气味义与颜色义借用的方式完全相同。

branches.en: The slang sense follows grass as a street name.
branches.cn: 俚语义跟随 grass 的街头别称而来。

branches.en: The slope you stand on and the smell you remember come from one noun.
branches.cn: 你脚踏的坡地与记住的气味，出自同一个名词。

intro.en: Grassy is a noun plus the adjective ending -y, and its own family runs to grassiness and to loose compounds made with looking.
intro.cn: grassy 是名词加形容词词尾 -y 构成的，它自己的词族延伸到 grassiness，以及用 looking 组成的松散复合词。

latinIntro.en: Grassy has no Latin relative; the nearest classical word for grass is uninvolved with the English ending -y.
latinIntro.cn: grassy 没有拉丁语同源词；拉丁语里表示草的词与英语后缀 -y 并无关联。

items.example: Grass is the stem of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: grass 是这一词族的词干。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms grassy and salty.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 grassy 与 salty。

items.example: Grassy drops the second s of grass before -y.
items.exampleCN: grassy 在加 -y 前省去了 grass 的第二个 s。

items.example: The -y changes to -i before -er.
items.exampleCN: 加 -er 前，词尾 -y 变为 -i。

items.example: The superlative ending is -iest.
items.exampleCN: 最高级词尾是 -iest。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms grassiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 grassiness。

items.example: Grassiness turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: grassiness 把形容词变成名词。

items.meaning: appearing to be covered with grass
items.example: Looking adds a seeming, not a fact.
items.exampleCN: 加上 looking 表示「看上去」而非事实。

items.meaningCN: 同型形容词（咸的、多云的、沙质的）
items.example: The pattern keeps grassy easy to decode.
items.exampleCN: 这一构词模式让 grassy 很容易拆解。

definition_zh: 使高兴；使满意；满足（欲望）；使如愿
definition_en: to please or satisfy someone, or to give in to a desire or curiosity
core_image: 一个愿望被轻轻接住，对方眼里露出笑意
scene: 孩子想要一本新画册，父亲当天就把它带回了家。The father gratified his young daughter by bringing home the picture book she had wanted for weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 gratify 是「使如愿、满足某人」的意思（第 1 个义项：使高兴、使满意）；句意：父亲满足小女儿的心愿，把她盼了好几个星期的画册带回了家。

pos.zh: 使高兴；使满意；满足（欲望或好奇心）

derivatives.zh: 由 gratify 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「满足；欣慰」
由现在分词形容词化，义为「令人欣慰的」
由过去分词形容词化，义为「感到满足的」
同源于拉丁语 gratis，义为「免费地」，与「恩惠」义相通

senses.title: To please or delight someone
senses.definition: to give someone pleasure or make someone feel satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到愉快或满意
senses.example: We were gratified to hear that our appeal had succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 听说我们的呼吁取得了成功，我们深感欣慰。
senses.why: The Latin root gratus means pleasing, so the verb names the act of making another person feel that pleasing state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 gratus 意为「令人愉快的」，所以这个词表示「让另一个人进入那种愉快状态」。

senses.title: To satisfy a desire or wish
senses.definition: to do what someone wants or to fulfil a strong desire
senses.definitionCN: 做某人想要的事，或满足强烈的欲望
senses.example: He gratified his craving for sweets with a large slice of cake.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一大块蛋糕满足了自己对甜食的渴望。
senses.why: A pleasing result comes from giving someone what they want, so the verb extends from pleasing a person to pleasing an appetite.
senses.whyCN: 让人愉快的效果往往来自「给出对方想要的东西」，于是动词从「使人愉快」扩展到「使欲望得到满足」。

senses.title: To feed a curiosity
senses.definition: to let a curiosity or impulse be expressed rather than resisted
senses.definitionCN: 让好奇心或冲动得到表达而不是被压制
senses.example: Readers who gratify their curiosity about the trial will find a lengthy account inside.
senses.exampleCN: 想要满足对这场审判的好奇心的读者，会在里面找到一大篇报道。
senses.why: Curiosity is a hunger of the mind, so pleasing it is another form of satisfying an appetite.
senses.whyCN: 好奇心是心灵上的饥饿，让好奇心得逞就是另一种「喂饱欲望」的说法。

senses.title: To give in to an impulse
senses.definition: to yield to a desire that is often seen as excessive or unwise
senses.definitionCN: 屈从于常被视为过度或不明智的欲望
senses.example: Critics say the paintings gratify the taste for spectacle at the cost of meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家说这些画迎合了追求奇观的口味，却牺牲了含义。
senses.why: Once satisfying a desire is granted freely, it shades into indulgence, where the granting itself becomes the criticism.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「满足欲望」被随意给予，含义就偏向「纵容」，被指责的正是这种轻易给予本身。

intro.en: Gratify comes from Latin gratus, pleasing or thankful, through the verb gratificari, to do a kindness.
intro.cn: gratify 源自拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的、感激的），经由动词 gratificari（施恩、做善事）进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to praise or welcome lies behind the Latin family.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个意为「称赞、欢迎」的重构词根是这组拉丁词的来源（重构形式，存疑）。

items.en: Gratus means pleasing, welcome, or thankful.
items.cn: gratus 意为令人愉快的、受欢迎的或心怀感激的。

items.en: Gratificari, from gratus and facere, means to do a favour or show kindness.
items.cn: gratificari 由 gratus 与 facere（做）构成，意为施恩、做好事。

items.en: English borrows the verb as gratify and narrows it to pleasing another person.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入该动词，写作 gratify，语义收窄为「使他人愉快」。

items.en: Later uses extend from pleasing a person to satisfying desires and curiosities.
items.cn: 后来的用法从「使人愉快」扩展到「满足欲望与好奇心」。

note.en: Gratify sits in the Latin family of gratitude and grace, next to English words for pleasing and satisfying.
note.cn: gratify 属于 gratitude、grace 这一拉丁词族，旁边是英语中表示「使愉快」与「满足」的词。

entries.definition: the pleasure of having a desire satisfied
entries.definitionCN: 满足感；欲望得到满足时的快感

entries.definition: feeling or showing thanks
entries.definitionCN: 感激的；表示感谢的

entries.definition: the feeling of being thankful
entries.definitionCN: 感激之情

entries.definition: to make oneself pleasing to someone in order to gain favour
entries.definitionCN: 讨好；逢迎（与 gratify 同出 gratus，但侧重取悦他人以谋利）

entries.definition: to make someone feel that a need or wish is met
entries.definitionCN: 使满意；满足需要

entries.definition: to make someone happy
entries.definitionCN: 使高兴；使愉快

entries.definition: to allow yourself or another special pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 纵情于；纵容

normalIntro.en: Gratify is the verb behind gratitude: to gratify someone is to put them in the thankful, pleased state from which gratitude grows.
normalIntro.cn: gratify 是 gratitude 背后的动词：使某人高兴，就是让对方进入「感激、满意」的状态。

normal.en: Gratification is the noun built from gratify with the suffix -ation.
normal.cn: 名词 gratification 由 gratify 加后缀 -ation 构成。

normal.en: Both grateful and gratitude keep the same gratus root of pleasing and thankful.
normal.cn: grateful 与 gratitude 都保留同一个 gratus 词根，意为「令人愉快、感激」。

normal.en: The fixed phrases gratify a desire and gratify curiosity are very common.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 gratify a desire 与 gratify curiosity 都非常常见。

normal.en: Be gratified is passive and slightly formal, as in we are gratified to learn that.
normal.cn: be gratified 是被动、略正式的用法，多见于「很高兴得知某事」这类正式声明。

normal.en: Ingratiate uses the same root but aims at gaining favour for oneself, not at pleasing another.
normal.cn: ingratiate 也来自同一词根，但目的是为自己换取好感，而不是使别人愉快。

abstract.en: Picture a child holding a desired toy, face lit with joy.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子抱着想要的玩具，脸上放光。

abstract.en: Picture a thirsty person finally setting down an empty glass.
abstract.cn: 想象口渴的人终于放下一个空杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a page that readers flip quickly just to see how the story ends.
abstract.cn: 想象读者飞快翻页，只为看看故事怎么结尾。

examples.en: She was gratified by the warm response of the audience.
examples.cn: 观众的热情回应让她感到欣慰。

examples.en: The company gratified customers by answering every letter within a day.
examples.cn: 这家公司做到每封信都在一天内回复，让顾客很满意。

examples.en: Advertisers aim to gratify the desire for status, not to inform buyers.
examples.cn: 广告商瞄准的是满足人们对地位的渴求，而不是为买家提供信息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格瑞特-派」——分发特别的小礼物（派），大家都高兴起来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的；心怀感激的）+ facere（做）→ 拉丁语 gratificari（施恩、讨人喜欢）→ 英语 gratify，核心义「让人进入愉快的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Gratify begins with pleasing a person, grows into satisfying a wish, then extends to curiosity and finally to outright indulgence.
sensesIntro.cn: gratify 从「使人愉快」出发，长成「满足愿望」，再扩展到「满足好奇心」，最后走到「纵情沉溺」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wish is received gently and the face relaxes into a smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：愿望被温和地接住，脸上舒展成笑容。

branches.en: Pleasing a person is the stable centre of the word.
branches.cn: 使人愉快是这个词最稳定的中心义。

branches.en: Satisfying a wish is pleasing viewed from the side of the desire.
branches.cn: 满足愿望是从欲望角度看的「使人愉快」。

branches.en: Curiosity is a mental hunger, so it can be gratified too.
branches.cn: 好奇心是精神上的饥饿，因此也能被满足。

branches.en: Indulgence is pleasure granted too freely, the critical edge of the word.
branches.cn: 沉溺是过于随意地给予快感，是这个词的批评性一面。

branches.en: All three hold a wish that someone decides to grant.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都包含一个被某人决定予以满足的愿望。

intro.en: Gratify is built on the Latin base grat-, with suffixes added in English to form nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: gratify 建立在拉丁词基 grat- 之上，英语又加后缀构成名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratus means pleasing or thankful, and facere means to make or do.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gratus 意为「令人愉快的、感激的」，facere 意为「做、使」。

items.meaningCN: 令人愉快的；受欢迎的；感激的
items.example: Gratus supplies the pleasing core of the word.
items.exampleCN: gratus 提供了这个词「令人愉快」的核心。

items.example: Facere adds the idea of doing something for someone.
items.exampleCN: facere 加入了「为人做事」的意思。

items.meaning: to do a kindness, to oblige
items.example: Gratificari is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: gratificari 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ify marks gratify as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ify 标明 gratify 是动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ation forms gratification.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 gratification。

items.example: Instant gratification is a common phrase in modern writing.
items.exampleCN: instant gratification 是现代写作中的常见搭配。

items.meaningCN: 表示「产生某种效果」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms the adjective gratifying.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成形容词 gratifying。

items.example: Grateful shows the gratus base in another branch.
items.exampleCN: grateful 展示了 gratus 词基的另一分支。

items.example: Ingratiate is built with the Latin prefix in-.
items.exampleCN: ingratiate 由拉丁前缀 in- 构成。

latinEntries.meaning: to oblige, to do a kindness

definition_zh: 无正当理由的；不必要的；无端的；免费的
definition_en: done without good reason and therefore unnecessary or offensive, or given without charge
core_image: 一份没有由来、凭空塞过来的东西
scene: 影评人说导演在片中加了一段与情节毫无关系的打斗。Critics said the fight scene was gratuitous and added nothing to the plot.
sceneCN: 这里 gratuitous 是「无理由的、多余的」（第 1 个义项：无正当理由而显得多余）；句意：评论家说这场打斗纯属多余，对情节毫无贡献。

pos.zh: 无正当理由的；不必要的；无端的；免费的

derivatives.zh: 由 gratuitous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「多余地；无端地」
同一拉丁词干的名词，义为「小费；酬金」
同源副词，义为「免费地」

senses.title: Unnecessary and without good reason
senses.titleCN: 不必要的；无正当理由的
senses.definition: added or done with no good reason, so the thing feels unnecessary
senses.definitionCN: 毫无正当理由地加入或做出，因此显得多余
senses.example: The editor cut several gratuitous scenes from the film.
senses.exampleCN: 剪辑师从影片中删掉了几场多余的戏。
senses.why: Latin gratuitus means given freely, and a gift that nobody asked for has no cause to justify it, so free turns into uncalled for.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gratuitus 意为「无偿给予的」；没人要的赠予找不到理由，于是「无偿」滑向「没有来由」。

senses.title: Shocking without being needed
senses.definition: describing violence, sex, or strong images that seem added only to shock
senses.definitionCN: 形容暴力、性等内容只是为了刺激观众而被生硬加入
senses.example: Parents complained about the gratuitous violence in the series.
senses.exampleCN: 家长们抱怨这部剧里充斥着无端的暴力场面。
senses.why: Violence or sex inserted to shock is the clearest case of content that arrives with no cause behind it.
senses.whyCN: 为刺激观众而硬塞进去的暴力或色情场面，是「无来由内容」最典型的例子。

senses.title: Given free of charge
senses.definition: given or done as a free favour with no payment expected
senses.definitionCN: 作为无偿恩惠给予或做出，不期待报酬
senses.example: The old word survives in the phrase a gratuitous service.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老义项保留在「无偿的服务」这一短语里。
senses.why: This is the oldest meaning: unnecessary and free amount to the same base, something that comes without a price attached.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：「多余」与「免费」出自同一个底子——「不附加任何代价」。

intro.en: Gratuitous comes from Latin gratuitus, free of charge, from gratia, favour or grace.
intro.cn: gratuitous 来自拉丁语 gratuitus（免费的），源于 gratia（恩惠、雅致）。

items.en: A reconstructed root often linked to praise or welcome underlies the Latin family, but the exact form is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为这组拉丁词源于一个与「称赞、欢迎」相关的重构词根，但具体形式存在争议（重构形式）。

items.en: Gratia means favour, goodwill, or grace.
items.cn: gratia 意为恩惠、善意或优雅。

items.en: Gratuitus is formed on gratia and means given freely or for nothing.
items.cn: gratuitus 由 gratia 构成，意为无偿给予的、免费的。

items.en: English borrows the adjective with the sense of free or without charge.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪借入该形容词，当时意为「免费的」。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the modern sense of unwarranted and uncalled for dominates.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，现代义「不必要的、无来由的」成为主导。

note.en: Gratuitous shares the Latin grat- family with gratitude and gratuity, and sits near words for needless or free.
note.cn: gratuitous 与 gratitude、gratuity 同属拉丁 grat- 词族，并与表示「多余」或「免费」的词相邻。

entries.definition: a tip given in addition to a bill
entries.definitionCN: 小费；额外酬金（与 gratuitous 同源，仍保留「无偿给予」的意思）

entries.definition: without payment
entries.definitionCN: 免费地（只在「免费」义上与 gratuitous 重合）

entries.definition: the pleasure of having a desire met
entries.definitionCN: 满足；欣慰（同出 gratia 词族，但义已偏向快感）

entries.definition: not justified or supported by facts
entries.definitionCN: 无正当理由的；无根据的

entries.definition: not needed
entries.definitionCN: 不必要的（中性词，不带 gratuitous 的批评色彩）

entries.definition: not required and avoidable
entries.definitionCN: 不必要的；可避免的

normalIntro.en: Gratuitous began as a word for something free and turned into a word for something that should not have been there.
normalIntro.cn: gratuitous 起初表示「免费的」，后来变成表示「本不该出现」的词。

normal.en: Gratuity is the tip you leave, the same free gift idea in noun form.
normal.cn: gratuity 是小费，是同一「无偿赠予」概念的名词形式。

normal.en: The adverb gratuitously usually follows verbs such as add, include, or insult.
normal.cn: 副词 gratuitously 常跟在 add、include、insult 等动词后。

normal.en: In film reviews the fixed phrase gratuitous violence is extremely common.
normal.cn: 在影评中，固定搭配 gratuitous violence 极为常见。

normal.en: Compare gratuitous with free: free is neutral, while gratuitous in the modern sense is critical.
normal.cn: 对比 free：free 是中性的，现代义项的 gratuitous 带有批评意味。

normal.en: The root grat- also appears in gratitude, grateful, and gratify.
normal.cn: 词根 grat- 也出现在 gratitude、grateful 与 gratify 中。

abstract.en: Picture an extra footnote in an essay that explains nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一篇论文里有一条什么也没解释的多余脚注。

abstract.en: Picture a loud explosion in a quiet drama that only startles the viewer.
abstract.cn: 想象一部安静的剧情片里突然一声巨响，只为了吓人。

abstract.en: Picture a gift left on a doorstep with no name and no price tag.
abstract.cn: 想象门口留下的一份礼物，没有名字，也没有价签。

examples.en: The article was full of gratuitous personal remarks about the author.
examples.cn: 这篇文章充满了对作者的无关人身评论。

examples.en: Cutting the gratuitous subplot made the novel much tighter.
examples.cn: 删掉那段多余的支线使小说紧凑了许多。

examples.en: It would be gratuitous to promise a result before the tests finish.
examples.cn: 测试还没结束就许诺结果是多此一举。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「古拉图伊特斯」——古拉画了一张图，图上伊特只是多余的涂鸦；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gratia（恩惠、善意）→ gratuitus（无偿给予的；免费的）→ 法语/英语借入后转义为「白给的、没来由的」→ 现代英语「无端的、多余的」。

sensesIntro.en: Gratuitous starts from something given for free, shifts from free to uncalled for, and ends with content added only to shock.
sensesIntro.cn: gratuitous 从「无偿给予」起家，由「免费」转为「没来由」，最后落到「只为刺激而添加的内容」与「无端的」用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a parcel arrives with no sender and no reason.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个包裹送到，没有寄件人，也没有理由。

branches.en: Needing no cause is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 「没有来由」是主要的现代义项。

branches.en: Content added only to shock takes the critical sense to extremes.
branches.cn: 只为刺激而添加的内容把批评性义项推到极端。

branches.en: The free sense is the historical base, kept alive mainly in specialist writing.
branches.cn: 「免费」义是历史基底，主要保留在专门写作中。

branches.en: Both senses judge the content as arriving without a reason.
branches.cn: 这两个义项都判定该内容属于「无理由出现」。

branches.en: Free and uncalled for were once one idea: something that comes with no price attached.
branches.cn: 「免费」与「多余」曾是同一个观念：不附带代价。

intro.en: Gratuitous is an adjective from the Latin noun gratia, and later English forms add -ly and -ity to build its family.
intro.cn: gratuitous 是由拉丁名词 gratia 派生出的形容词，后来英语又加 -ly 与 -ity 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratia means favour or grace, and the adjective gratuitus means given freely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gratia 意为恩惠或雅致，形容词 gratuitus 意为无偿给予的。

items.example: Gratia is the base of the whole grat- family.
items.exampleCN: gratia 是整个 grat- 词族的基础。

items.example: Gratuitus is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: gratuitus 是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous marks the word as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 标明该词是形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms gratuitously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 gratuitously。

items.example: The adverb usually criticises an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常用于批评某种行为。

items.meaningCN: 源自拉丁语的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ous marks an adjective formed from a Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 标示由拉丁词干构成的形容词。

items.example: Gratuity keeps the free gift sense.
items.exampleCN: gratuity 保留了「无偿赠予」的义项。

items.example: The suffix -ness could form an abstract noun, but it is rare here.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 可构成抽象名词，但在这个词上很少见。

items.example: The ending of gratuitus explains the final -ous in English.
items.exampleCN: gratuitus 的词尾解释了英语中结尾的 -ous。

definition_zh: 砾石；碎石；铺砾石；（旧）使困惑；肾结石
definition_en: small stones used for roads and paths, or to spread such stones on a surface
core_image: 一把指甲盖大小的碎石哗啦落在路面上
scene: 园丁把一车细石铺在车道入口。The gardener spread a load of gravel along the driveway.
sceneCN: 这里 gravel 是「碎石、砾石」（第 1 个义项：铺路用的小石子）；句意：园丁把一车碎石铺在车道边。

derivatives.zh: 由 gravel 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「布满砾石的；（嗓音）沙哑的」
由 gravel 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「铺砾石的工作」
由过去分词形容词化，义为「铺了碎石的」

senses.title: Small loose stones
senses.definition: small loose stones worn or broken from rock, used on roads and paths
senses.definitionCN: 由岩石磨碎或崩解成的小石子，常用于道路与小径
senses.example: The children scattered gravel across the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把碎石撒得满操场都是。
senses.why: The word names the material itself, the loose stones gathered from river beds or pits.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指材料本身——从河床或砂坑里收集来的散碎石子。

senses.title: A surface that crunches and slips
senses.definition: the ground or road covered by such small stones
senses.definitionCN: 由这种小石子铺成的地面或道路
senses.example: Their footsteps made a soft sound on the gravel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的脚步在砾石上发出轻柔的沙沙声。
senses.why: Once the stones are laid down, the surface made of them can be called by the name of the material.
senses.whyCN: 石子铺好之后，由它们构成的地面就用材料的名字来称呼，这是转喻。

senses.title: To cover a surface with gravel
senses.definition: to spread or cover a path or drive with small stones
senses.definitionCN: 用碎石铺设或覆盖小径、车道
senses.example: They gravelled the yard before laying the lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在铺草坪之前先把院子铺上了碎石。
senses.why: The noun is used as a verb when the material is applied to a place.
senses.whyCN: 当这种材料被施加到某处时，名词就转作动词使用。

senses.title: A rough, harsh voice
senses.definition: causing a rough crackling sound, as if small stones were being shifted
senses.definitionCN: 发出如小石子摩擦般的粗糙沙哑声响
senses.example: He answered in a low gravel voice that surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他低声回答，嗓音粗哑，让大家都吃了一惊。
senses.why: The texture of loose stone is borrowed for sound: the rough edges become a rough voice.
senses.whyCN: 把碎石粗糙的质感借来形容声音：砾石的棱角变成了粗哑的音色。

senses.title: To puzzle or disconcert
senses.definition: an older use meaning to confuse, annoy, or get someone into a tight spot
senses.definitionCN: 一种较古老的用法，意为使人困惑、恼怒或陷入困境
senses.example: In old novels villains are often gravelled for an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧小说里，反派人物常被问得哑口无言。
senses.why: Gravel jams a wheel, so to be gravelled is to be stuck, and the old sense names a person stuck for an answer.
senses.whyCN: 砾石会卡住车轮，所以「被砾石困住」就是「被困住」，古老义项用来形容人卡在那里答不上来。

intro.en: Gravel is usually explained via Old French gravele, a bed of sand, from a pre-Latin Alpine root on a stone or gravel word; the earliest English form is not fully certain.
intro.cn: gravel 一般认为经由古法语 gravele（沙砾床）而来，源于阿尔卑斯山区一个前拉丁词的「石、砾」词根；英语最早的形式并不完全确定。

items.en: A reconstructed Alpine root grav- for stone or gravel is proposed as the base, but its form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为底层是一个阿尔卑斯山区重构词根 grav-，表示「石、砾」，但具体形式存疑。

items.en: Latin borrowed the root in words such as grava and gravelle, a gravel pit.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 grava、gravelle（砾石坑）等词借入该词根。

items.en: Gravele names a bed of sand or coarse gravel.
items.cn: 古法语 gravele 指沙砾层或粗砾。

items.en: English gravele names the loose stones used on roads.
items.cn: 中古英语 gravele 指铺路用的散碎石子。

items.en: The verb meaning to cover with gravel and the older sense of to puzzle both become established.
items.cn: 动词「铺碎石」和「使困惑」的古老义项先后确立。

note.en: Gravel is a size word: coarser than sand, finer than shingle, and close to the whole family of stone terms.
note.cn: gravel 是一个「尺寸词」：比砂大，比卵石小，并与大量「石」类词相邻。

entries.definition: full of gravel, or rough sounding
entries.definitionCN: 布满砾石的；嗓音粗哑的

entries.definition: a place where a body is buried
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓；只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自古英语 graf）

entries.definition: having no grave
entries.definitionCN: 没有坟墓的；这里 grave 指坟墓，与砾石无关

entries.definition: a small smooth stone worn by water
entries.definitionCN: 鹅卵石；被水磨圆的小石子

entries.definition: coarse gravel on a beach
entries.definitionCN: （海滩上的）卵石；粗砾

entries.definition: fine loose grains of worn rock
entries.definitionCN: 沙；比砾石颗粒更细的碎屑

normalIntro.en: Gravel is a material word, so it is best kept with its sizes and its surfaces.
normalIntro.cn: gravel 是一个材料词，最好和它的尺寸、铺面一起记。

normal.en: Gravel sits between sand and pebbles in size.
normal.cn: gravel 的颗粒介于沙子和鹅卵石之间。

normal.en: Gravelly keeps the rough texture for both ground and voice.
normal.cn: gravelly 把粗糙质感同时用于地面和嗓音。

normal.en: The British spelling doubles the l, as in gravelled, while American spelling keeps one l.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，如 gravelled；美式拼写只写一个 l。

normal.en: A gravel pit is the place where the stones are dug out.
normal.cn: gravel pit 就是挖取砾石的场所。

normal.en: Sand and gravel are often listed together because they are used in concrete and road work.
normal.cn: sand and gravel 常一起出现，因为二者都用于混凝土与道路工程。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of tiny grey stones sliding off a palm.
abstract.cn: 想象一小把灰色小石子从掌心滑落。

abstract.en: Hear shoes crunch over a dry stone path in summer.
abstract.cn: 听见夏日里鞋子踩过干石头小路的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Picture a wheelbarrow tipped forward to spread the stones.
abstract.cn: 想象独轮车向前一倾，石子撒了出去。

examples.en: The path to the cottage was covered in loose gravel.
examples.cn: 通往小屋的小路上铺着松散的碎石。

examples.en: Workers gravelled the new car park over the summer.
examples.cn: 工人们在夏天把新停车场铺上了碎石。

examples.en: Her gravel voice made the old song sound strangely moving.
examples.cn: 她沙哑的嗓音让这首老歌听起来格外动人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格瑞-欧」——举筛子一抖，格子的石粒欧地一声全落下来，就是碎石；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 前拉丁（阿尔卑斯山区，重构形式，存疑）grav-（石、砾）→ 拉丁语 grava/gravelle → 古法语 gravele → 中古英语 gravele → 现代英语 gravel。

sensesIntro.en: Gravel starts as the name of the material, moves to the ground it covers and the act of covering, then lends its roughness to voice and its obstruction to the old sense of being stuck.
sensesIntro.cn: gravel 先是材料名，再指被它铺成的地面与铺的动作，然后借其粗糙形容嗓音，最后以「被卡住」引申出古老的「使困惑」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of small grey stones falling onto a path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把灰色小石子落在小路上。

branches.en: The material itself is the core sense.
branches.cn: 材料本身是核心义项。

branches.en: The ground covered by the stones is a metonymic stretch.
branches.cn: 以材料代指所铺地面，是转喻延伸。

branches.en: Covering a surface turns the noun into a verb.
branches.cn: 给表面铺上碎石，使名词转为动词。

branches.en: Rough texture gives the voice sense, and the stuck feeling gives the old sense of being puzzled.
branches.cn: 粗糙质感生出嗓音义，被卡住的感觉则生出「使困惑」的古老义。

branches.en: All three stay within the physical world of stones.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都停留在石子的物理世界里。

intro.en: Gravel is a short, root-based word; its English family is built by adding -ly, -ing, and past-participle endings.
intro.cn: gravel 是一个以词根为基础的短词，其英语词族靠加 -ly、-ing 与过去分词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The base is a reconstructed pre-Latin Alpine word for stone, taken up by Latin as grava.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是一个表示「石」的前拉丁阿尔卑斯山区重构词，被拉丁语吸收为 grava。

items.example: The root grav- is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 grav- 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Latin grava carries the rough material sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 grava 保留了粗糙材料义。

items.meaning: a bed of sand or coarse gravel
items.example: Old French gravele likely supplies the English form.
items.exampleCN: 英语形式很可能来自古法语 gravele。

items.example: Gravel keeps the material sense in English.
items.exampleCN: gravel 在英语中保留材料义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms gravelly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 gravelly。

items.meaning: covered with gravel, or rough sounding
items.example: Gravelly describes both ground and voice.
items.exampleCN: gravelly 可形容地面和嗓音。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms gravelling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 gravelling。

items.meaningCN: 过去分词或「具有」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ed forms gravelled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 gravelled。

items.meaning: a place where gravel is dug
items.example: The compound gravel-pit names the extraction site.
items.exampleCN: 合成词 gravel-pit 指采掘场所。

latinEntries.meaning: a pit of sand or gravel

definition_zh: （牲畜）吃草；放牧；擦伤；擦过
definition_en: to eat grass in a field, to put animals to eat grass, or to touch a surface lightly and scrape the skin
core_image: 牛群低着头在草坡上慢慢移动，牙齿贴着草尖；另一只手擦过粗糙的石壁，蹭破一层皮
scene: 暮色里，牧人把羊群赶上山坡，草叶被啃得齐整。At dusk the shepherd let the sheep graze on the open hillside.
sceneCN: 这里 graze 是「（牲畜）吃草」（第 1 个义项：牛马羊等在地里吃草）；句意为黄昏时牧人让羊群在开阔的山坡上吃草。画面里有草坡、羊群和渐渐暗下来的天空。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 名词化构成，义为「放牧；牧场」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「食草动物；放牧者」
由前缀 over- 加本词构成，义为「过度放牧」
法律用语，指「受托代牧；放牧权」，说的就是把牲畜托给别人草地吃草

senses.title: To eat grass in a field
senses.definition: to eat grass or small plants growing in a field, as cattle, sheep or horses do
senses.definitionCN: 像牛、羊、马那样在地里吃草或低矮植物
senses.example: A few cows were grazing quietly on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 几头牛在山坡上安静地吃草。
senses.why: The Old English verb grasian comes from graes, grass, so the core act is simply feeding on grass.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 grasian 由 graes（草）派生而来，所以核心动作就是吃草。

senses.title: To put animals out to feed
senses.definition: to take farm animals to a field and let them feed there
senses.definitionCN: 把家畜带到地里，让它们在那里吃草
senses.example: Farmers graze their goats on the common land.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫们在公共草地上放羊。
senses.why: If the animals graze, the person who sends them there also grazes them, so the verb shifts from the eater to the keeper.
senses.whyCN: 牲畜在吃草，把牲畜赶去吃草的人也就「放牧」，动词的主体从被吃的动物转向了照管的人。

senses.title: To scrape the skin
senses.definition: to break or scrape the surface of the skin slightly
senses.definitionCN: 轻微地擦破皮肤表层
senses.example: She fell off her bike and grazed her elbow.
senses.exampleCN: 她从自行车上摔下来，擦伤了胳膊肘。
senses.why: This sense has a different origin, from English grass, and pictures a body brushing along the ground like an animal mouthing grass.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同，一般认为与英语 grass 有关，画面是身体沿着地面蹭过去，就像牲口咬过草面。

senses.title: To touch lightly in passing
senses.definition: to touch or brush against something lightly and quickly while moving
senses.definitionCN: 移动时轻而快地碰到或擦过某物
senses.example: The branch grazed the side of the passing truck.
senses.exampleCN: 树枝擦过了驶过的卡车侧面。
senses.why: Once grazing means skimming a surface, the image extends to any object that brushes past another without stopping.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「擦过」意味着贴着表面掠过，这个意象就扩展到任何不停留的轻触。

senses.title: Land used for grazing
senses.definition: land that animals are kept on so that they can eat the grass
senses.definitionCN: 供牲畜吃草的牧场或草地
senses.example: The valley has rich grazing for sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷有供羊吃草的肥沃牧场。
senses.why: The -ing form turns the action into a place, so grazing names the pasture where the eating happens.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式把动作变为场所，于是 grazing 就指吃草这件事发生的牧场。

intro.en: Graze has two unrelated histories that now share one spelling: eating grass comes from Old English graes, while scraping the skin probably comes from grass as a word for ground.
intro.cn: graze 有两段互不相干的来历，如今共用同一拼写：吃草义来自古英语 graes（草），擦伤义一般认为与表示地面的 grass 有关。

items.en: Graes means grass, and the weak verb grasian means to feed on grass.
items.cn: graes 意为草，弱变化动词 grasian 意为吃草。

items.en: The spellings graze and grase appear, and the sense of putting animals to feed develops.
items.cn: 出现 graze、grase 等拼写，并发展出「放牲畜吃草」的意思。

items.en: Graze is recorded in the sense of scraping or rubbing the skin, generally linked to grass as ground.
items.cn: 十七世纪记录到 graze 表示擦伤、蹭破皮肤；一般认为与表示地面的 grass 有关。

items.en: The light touch sense appears, describing a bullet or branch that just brushes a surface.
items.cn: 十八世纪出现轻触义，用于描述子弹或树枝只是擦过表面。

items.en: Both branches settle on one spelling, and grazing becomes the standard term for pasture.
items.cn: 两条分支最终落在同一拼写上，grazing 成为牧场与放牧的标准说法。

note.en: Graze belongs to the pasture field of graze, grazer and grazing, and stands beside feed, nibble and scrape.
note.cn: graze 属于牧场词族（graze、grazer、grazing），并与 feed、nibble、scrape 等词相邻。

entries.definition: the green plant that covers fields and lawns
entries.definitionCN: 草地上的绿色植物；草，是吃草义的词根来源

entries.definition: the act of feeding animals on grass, or the pasture they use
entries.definitionCN: 放牧；牧场

entries.definition: an animal that feeds mainly on grass
entries.definitionCN: 食草动物；放牧者

entries.definition: to put a shiny coat on pottery or food
entries.definitionCN: 给陶器或食物上釉、挂糖；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to give food to a person or animal, or to eat food
entries.definitionCN: 喂养；进食，范围比 graze 更广

entries.definition: to take small repeated bites
entries.definitionCN: 小口小口地啃咬

entries.definition: of animals, to eat leaves and shoots from trees
entries.definitionCN: （牲畜）啃食枝叶，与在林间吃草的 graze 相对

entries.definition: to rub against a hard surface and damage the skin
entries.definitionCN: 刮擦；蹭伤，对应擦伤义

normalIntro.en: Graze ties grass to teeth and to a light scrape: the same spelling carries eating and touching.
normalIntro.cn: graze 把草、牙齿和轻轻的擦碰连在一起：同一个拼写既表示吃草，也表示擦碰。

normal.en: Graze comes from Old English graes, grass, so a grazing animal is one that lives on grass.
normal.cn: graze 来自古英语 graes（草），所以吃草的动物就是以草为生的动物。

normal.en: Cattle graze on the hillside means the animals eat there and the owner lets them.
normal.cn: 「cattle graze on the hillside」既指牛在山坡吃草，也指主人把牛放养在那里。

normal.en: To graze your knee is to take a light scrape, close to the word scrape.
normal.cn: 「graze your knee」是轻轻擦伤膝盖，与 scrape 意思贴近。

normal.en: A bullet that grazes a wall touches it only for an instant.
normal.cn: 子弹「graze」过墙面，只是在一瞬间碰到了墙。

normal.en: Compare browse: cattle graze on grass, deer browse on leaves and shoots.
normal.cn: 对比 browse：牛在地面吃草是 graze，鹿啃食枝叶是 browse。

abstract.en: Picture a slow row of backs moving through green, heads never higher than the knees.
abstract.cn: 想象一排背脊缓缓穿过绿色，头始终不高于膝盖。

abstract.en: Imagine a farmer waving his flock towards a far field at sunset.
abstract.cn: 想象夕阳下农夫把羊群朝远处的田里赶去。

abstract.en: Think of a falling cyclist whose elbow just kisses the gravel without a full impact.
abstract.cn: 想象摔车的骑手胳膊肘只是轻轻蹭到碎石，并没有重重撞上。

examples.en: Horses graze in the meadow behind the farm.
examples.cn: 马在农场后面的草场上吃草。

examples.en: The goalkeeper grazed the post with his shoulder.
examples.cn: 守门员的肩膀擦到了门柱。

examples.en: She grazed her arm on the rough stone wall.
examples.cn: 她的手臂蹭到了粗糙的石墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格瑞兹」——像「哥了兹」：哥哥低头在草地上啃草，牙齿蹭着草叶；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 graes（草）→ grasian（吃草）→ 中古英语 grazen；擦伤义一般认为另源自表示地面的 grass，两条来路汇成现代 graze。

sensesIntro.en: Graze starts with animals eating grass, widens to the farmer who puts them out, then splits into a scrape of skin and a passing touch, and ends with the pasture itself.
sensesIntro.cn: graze 从牲畜吃草出发，扩展到农夫放牧，再分出擦伤皮肤与擦过掠过两个义项，最后落到牧场这个地点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heads bent to the grass, teeth just brushing it.
core.cn: 核心意象：头低向草地，牙齿轻轻擦过草尖。

branches.en: The everyday sense is livestock eating grass in a field.
branches.cn: 日常义项是牲畜在地里吃草。

branches.en: The keeper who sends the animals out is the second sense.
branches.cn: 把牲畜赶去吃草的人对应放牧义项。

branches.en: The scrape on skin and the passing touch are two forms of brushing a surface.
branches.cn: 擦伤皮肤与擦过掠过是「贴着表面轻碰」的两种表现。

branches.en: The action of eating and the ground where it happens name each other.
branches.cn: 吃草的动作与发生这动作的土地互为名称。

branches.en: A farmer with land for grazing and land with animals on it are one practice.
branches.cn: 有地的农夫与地上有牲畜是同一件事情的两面。

intro.en: Graze has no classical prefix or suffix; English builds grazing, grazer and overgraze around its Old English base for grass.
intro.cn: graze 没有古典前缀或后缀；英语围绕它表示「草」的古英语词干构成 grazing、grazer、overgraze。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin word behind the grass sense: the root is Old English graes, so the family is Germanic rather than classical.
latinIntro.cn: 吃草义背后没有拉丁语词：词根是古英语 graes，因此整个词族属于日耳曼语而非古典语。

items.example: Graes names the plant the animals eat.
items.exampleCN: graes 指牲畜所吃的植物。

items.example: Grasian is the direct Old English parent.
items.exampleCN: grasian 是直接的古英语前身。

items.example: Graze keeps the eating sense.
items.exampleCN: graze 保留了吃草义。

items.meaning: the act or place of doing
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或场所的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms grazing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 grazing。

items.meaning: pasture, or the act of feeding on grass
items.example: Grazing names the pasture as well as the act.
items.exampleCN: grazing 既指放牧，也指牧场。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms grazer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 grazer。

items.example: Grazer points at the animal itself.
items.exampleCN: grazer 直接指动物本身。

items.example: The prefix over- marks too much grazing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 表示放牧过度。

items.meaning: to put so many animals on a field that it is damaged
items.example: Overgraze describes ruined pasture.
items.exampleCN: overgraze 描述被破坏的草场。

definition_zh: 油腻的；含脂肪的；滑腻的；油腔滑调的
definition_en: covered with or containing oil or fat, slippery to touch, or behaving in a smooth way that seems insincere
core_image: 指尖从沾满油的盘沿滑过去，留下一道亮亮的油光；有些人说话时也像这样滑得抓不住
scene: 餐馆打烊后，后厨的盘子和灶台都蒙着一层油。The cook wiped the greasy surface of the stove with a cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 greasy 是「油腻的、泛着油的」（第 1 个义项：表面沾满油脂）；句意为厨师用布擦掉灶台上那层油光的表面。画面里有挂油光的灶台、抹布和一排待洗的盘子。

pos.zh: 油腔滑调的；过分讨好的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词去尾构成的基础名词，义为「油脂；润滑脂」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「油腻；油滑」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「油腻地；油滑地」
由前缀 de- 加名词 grease 构成，义为「除油；脱脂」

senses.title: Covered with oil or fat
senses.definition: covered with or full of oil or fat, especially in a way that feels unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 表面或内部充满油脂，常给人不舒服的感觉
senses.example: These plates are still greasy after washing.
senses.exampleCN: 这些盘子洗过之后还是油腻腻的。
senses.why: The suffix -y builds an adjective meaning full of, so greasy describes a thing that has absorbed oil or fat until it feels unclean.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 构成「充满……」的形容词，所以 greasy 描述的是一样东西吸满了油，变得不干净。

senses.title: Rich in fat as food
senses.definition: containing a lot of fat or oil, used of food that may be heavy or unhealthy
senses.definitionCN: 食物中含大量脂肪或油，往往被认为厚重或不健康
senses.example: He cut greasy chips and fried food from his diet.
senses.exampleCN: 他把油腻的薯条和煎炸食物从饮食中去掉了。
senses.why: Food is the most familiar carrier of oil, so the tactile sense moves easily to what we eat and its health effects.
senses.whyCN: 食物是油脂最常见的去处，所以触觉义很容易转移到我们吃的东西及其健康影响上。

senses.title: Slippery to the touch
senses.definition: slippery because of oil, so that it is hard to hold or stand on
senses.definitionCN: 因为沾了油而很滑，难以握住或站稳
senses.example: The path was greasy with rain and old cooking oil.
senses.exampleCN: 小路被雨水和倒下的废油弄得滑腻腻的。
senses.why: Oil has long been used to make machines move freely, so the physical slipperiness of oil becomes a separate sense.
senses.whyCN: 很久以来人们用油让机械运转自如，于是油带来的物理滑溜成为独立义项。

senses.title: Insincerely smooth in manner
senses.titleCN: 油腔滑调的；过分讨好的
senses.definition: speaking or behaving in a smooth, overly friendly way that does not seem genuine
senses.definitionCN: 说话或举止圆滑、过分亲热，显得不真诚
senses.example: The salesman gave a greasy smile and promised everything.
senses.exampleCN: 那个推销员露出谄媚的笑，什么都一口答应。
senses.why: A slippery surface cannot be gripped, and a slippery manner cannot be pinned down, so physical grease becomes social smoothness.
senses.whyCN: 滑溜溜的表面抓不住，滑头滑脑的姿态也把握不住，于是物理上的油滑变成了社交上的圆滑。

senses.title: Unpolished and cheap, of places
senses.definition: used of small cheap restaurants or places that serve simple fried food and feel shabby
senses.definitionCN: 形容供应简单煎炸食物的小饭馆或地方，有寒酸、油腻之感
senses.example: We ate at a greasy little cafe near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近一家油腻的小咖啡馆吃饭。
senses.why: The phrase greasy spoon ties fried food to cheapness, and the adjective then describes whole places of that kind.
senses.whyCN: 「greasy spoon」把煎炸食物与廉价联系起来，这个形容词于是也能描述整类这样的地方。

intro.en: Greasy is the adjective from grease, a word of uncertain origin whose spelling was shaped by Old French craisse and gresse.
intro.cn: greasy 由 grease 派生而来；grease 的来源不确定，其拼写受古法语 craisse 与 gresse 影响。

items.en: Craisse and gresse mean fat or grease, from Latin crassus, thick or solid fat.
items.cn: craisse 与 gresse 意为油脂，源自拉丁语 crassus（浓稠的脂肪）。

items.en: Grece appears in English for animal fat, with the spelling later settling as grease.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语出现 grece，指动物脂肪，后来拼写固定为 grease。

items.en: The adjective greasy forms with the suffix -y meaning full of.
items.cn: 形容词 greasy 以后缀 -y（充满……）构成。

items.en: The figurative sense of a smooth, insincere manner is recorded in writing.
items.cn: 表示圆滑、不真诚的比喻义在文字中留下记录。

items.en: Greasy extends to food, hair, roads, and the informal greasy spoon for a cheap diner.
items.cn: greasy 扩展到食物、头发、道路，并衍生出 greasy spoon 指廉价小饭馆。

note.en: Greasy belongs to the grease family and sits beside oil, fatty and slippery, which divide the same ground.
note.cn: greasy 属于 grease 词族，与 oil、fatty、slippery 相邻，这些词瓜分了同一片意义。

entries.definition: thick oil used for cooking or for making machines run
entries.definitionCN: 烹饪或润滑机械用的油脂，是 greasy 的基础名词

entries.definition: the quality of being greasy
entries.definitionCN: 油腻；油滑

entries.definition: in a greasy or insincere manner
entries.definitionCN: 油腻地；油滑地

entries.definition: not a standard word; a misspelling of grease
entries.definitionCN: 并非标准词，只是 grease 的错拼；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: covered in or containing oil, and also used of an insincere manner
entries.definitionCN: 沾油的；也指圆滑做作的

entries.definition: containing a lot of fat, used mainly of food
entries.definitionCN: 多脂肪的，多用于食物

entries.definition: difficult to hold or stand on because it is smooth and wet
entries.definitionCN: 滑的；易打滑的

entries.definition: too friendly in a way that is not sincere
entries.definitionCN: 油嘴滑舌、过分亲热的，与 greasy 的比喻义相近

normalIntro.en: Greasy is grease plus the full-of suffix, and its two lives are a surface you cannot grip and a manner you cannot trust.
normalIntro.cn: greasy 是 grease 加上「充满」后缀而来，它的两副面孔一是抓不住的表面，二是信不过的作风。

normal.en: Grease is the noun for fat and oil, and -y means full of, so greasy means full of fat.
normal.cn: grease 是油脂，-y 表示充满，所以 greasy 就是满是油脂。

normal.en: Greasy is pronounced with s, while the verb to grease ends in a z sound.
normal.cn: 形容词 greasy 的 s 读清音，而动词 grease 结尾读浊的 z 音。

normal.en: Greases and greased belong to the verb grease, not to the adjective greasy.
normal.cn: greases、greased 属于动词 grease，不属于形容词 greasy。

normal.en: Greasy spoon is a fixed phrase for a small cheap diner that fries its food.
normal.cn: greasy spoon 是固定说法，指只做煎炸的廉价小饭馆。

normal.en: Compare oily: greasy stresses the greasy feel on a surface, oily covers both oil and insincerity more broadly.
normal.cn: 对比 oily：greasy 更强调表面的油腻触感，oily 则更宽泛地兼指油和圆滑。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip sliding along a wet plate rim and leaving a bright line.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖沿着湿油的盘沿滑过，留下一道亮线。

abstract.en: Imagine a paper bag going dark and see-through where the fried food touches it.
abstract.cn: 想象装煎炸食物的纸袋，被浸得发暗透明。

abstract.en: Think of a shop assistant whose smile will not stay in your memory, like wet soap.
abstract.cn: 想象一名店员的笑容像沾了水的肥皂，怎么也攥不在记忆里。

examples.en: His hands were greasy after fixing the engine.
examples.cn: 修完发动机后，他的手沾满了油。

examples.en: The floor was greasy and people kept slipping.
examples.cn: 地面油腻打滑，人们不断滑倒。

examples.en: Doctors advise children to avoid greasy snacks.
examples.cn: 医生建议孩子少吃油腻的零食。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格里兹」——像「哥里滋」：油锅里滋啦一响，一股油腻味冒出来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 crassus（浓稠脂肪）→ 古法语 craisse、gresse → 英语 grease（油脂）→ 加后缀 -y 构成 greasy，核心义「布满油脂」。

sensesIntro.en: Greasy first names a surface or food full of fat, then the slipperiness that fat creates, and finally the untrustworthy smoothness of a person or a place.
sensesIntro.cn: greasy 先指布满油脂的表面或食物，再指油脂造成的滑腻，最后指人或场所令人信不过的圆滑与寒酸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip sliding across a plate and leaving a bright wet line.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖滑过盘子，留下一道亮亮的油痕。

branches.en: A greasy object is one covered in fat.
branches.cn: 沾满油脂的物体是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Greasy food is the same fat inside what we eat.
branches.cn: 油腻食物是同样的油脂进入了我们吃的东西。

branches.en: Sliding underfoot is the physical result of oil.
branches.cn: 脚下打滑是油脂造成的物理结果。

branches.en: A manner that cannot be gripped mirrors a surface that cannot be held.
branches.cn: 抓不住的作风对应握不住的表面。

branches.en: Fried food and the cheap places that serve it are named by one adjective.
branches.cn: 煎炸食物和供应它的廉价场所共用同一个形容词。

intro.en: Greasy is grease plus the suffix -y, and the family grows with -ness, -ly and the reversing prefix de-.
intro.cn: greasy 是 grease 加后缀 -y 构成，词族再通过 -ness、-ly 和表反义的前缀 de- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The medieval fat noun traces back to Latin crassus, thick or solid, entered English through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪的油脂名词可上溯到拉丁语 crassus（浓稠、实心），经古法语进入英语。

items.example: Crassus describes thick solid fat.
items.exampleCN: crassus 描述浓稠厚实的脂肪。

items.example: Craisse is the early French form.
items.exampleCN: craisse 是早期法语形式。

items.example: Grease keeps the base sense.
items.exampleCN: grease 保留基础义。

items.example: The suffix -y forms greasy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 greasy。

items.example: Greasy makes the noun into a quality.
items.exampleCN: greasy 把名词变成一种性质。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms greasiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 greasiness。

items.example: Greasiness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: greasiness 指这种性质。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms greasily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 greasily。

items.example: The prefix de- marks removing grease.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 表示去除油脂。

items.example: Degrease is the opposite direction.
items.exampleCN: degrease 表示反向操作。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 粗鄙的；愚钝的，与油滑义可对照

definition_zh: 爱社交的；合群的；（动物）群居的
definition_en: fond of being with other people, or of animals or plants, growing or living together in groups
core_image: 一群人挤在同一张桌子旁说笑，鸦群一起落在同一片树冠上
scene: 机场候机厅里，她从不独自坐着，总爱围着陌生人聊上一路。She was gregarious and soon knew every passenger in the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 gregarious 是「爱社交的、合群的」（第 1 个义项：喜欢与人相处）；句意为她既爱交友，很快就认识了候机厅里每一位乘客。画面里有候机长椅、行李和一群围着说话的人。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「合群地；群居地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「合群性；群居性」
罕见的同源形容词，义为「群居的；成群结队的」
由前缀 se-（分开）加 grex（群）构成，义为「隔离；分开」

senses.title: Fond of company
senses.definition: enjoying the company of other people and spending little time alone
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢与他人相处，很少独处
senses.example: She is gregarious and makes friends wherever she goes.
senses.exampleCN: 她性格合群，走到哪里都能交到朋友。
senses.why: Latin grex means a flock, and the suffix -arius means belonging to, so a gregarious person belongs to the flock by habit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 grex 意为「群」，后缀 -arius 表示「属于」，所以 gregarious 的人习性上就属于群体。

senses.title: Living in groups, of animals
senses.definition: used of animals that live together in flocks, herds or colonies rather than alone
senses.definitionCN: 形容动物成群结队、成群落居，而非独自生活
senses.example: Elephants are gregarious and move in large family groups.
senses.exampleCN: 大象是群居动物，以庞大的家族群活动。
senses.why: The flock at the heart of the word becomes literal again in biology, where herds and colonies are the original group.
senses.whyCN: 词根里的「群」在生物学语境中又变回字面意思：兽群、鸟群、群落就是最本来的群体。

senses.title: Growing in clusters, of plants
senses.definition: used of plants that grow in dense clusters or close groups
senses.definitionCN: 形容植物成簇密集地生长在一起
senses.example: This gregarious grass spreads into thick mats.
senses.exampleCN: 这种成簇生长的草会铺成厚厚的一层。
senses.why: Botany extends the flock to the garden bed, where separate plants crowd together and grow as one patch.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把「群」扩展到花圃里：原本分开的植株挤在一起，长成同一片。

senses.title: Of a sociable nature
senses.definition: describing a habit or instinct that draws a creature towards a group
senses.definitionCN: 描述把生物吸引向群体的习惯或本能
senses.example: Humans have a gregarious instinct that shaped early villages.
senses.exampleCN: 人类有群居本能，这种本能塑造了早期的村落。
senses.why: When the trait is looked at from inside, as a drive, the adjective names the instinct rather than the behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 当把这种特质看作内在驱动力时，形容词指的就是本能而非外在行为。

senses.title: Sociable gatherings
senses.definition: used of places or occasions that are lively and full of social mixing
senses.definitionCN: 形容场所或场合热闹、充满社交互动
senses.example: The club offers a gregarious evening of food and talk.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部提供一场伴着美食与畅谈的热闹夜晚。
senses.why: If a person is gregarious, the event that brings people together is gregarious by extension.
senses.whyCN: 如果人合群，那么把人聚到一起的场合也就由延伸而得到了同样形容。

intro.en: Gregarious comes from Latin grex, gregis, a flock or herd, with the suffix -arius meaning belonging to.
intro.cn: gregarious 来自拉丁语 grex（属格 gregis，兽群、鸟群），加上后缀 -arius（属于……的）。

items.en: The reconstructed root ger means to gather or collect, behind many words for a crowd.
items.cn: 重构词根 ger 意为聚集、收集，是许多表示人群的词背后共同的来源。

items.en: Grex means a flock or herd, and gregarius means belonging to a flock.
items.cn: grex 意为兽群、鸟群，gregarius 意为属于群体。

items.en: The adjective enters English first with the animal sense of living in herds.
items.cn: 形容词最初以「成群生活」的动物义进入英语。

items.en: The modern human sense of fond of company is recorded.
items.cn: 记录下现代用于人「喜欢与人相处」的含义。

items.en: Botany and sociology adopt the word for clustered plants and social instinct.
items.cn: 植物学与社会学借用了这个词，分别表示成簇植物与群居本能。

note.en: Gregarious shares the Latin flock with aggregate, segregate and congregate, and stands beside sociable and outgoing.
note.cn: gregarious 与 aggregate、segregate、congregate 共享拉丁语「群」的意象，与 sociable、outgoing 词义相邻。

entries.definition: to come together in a crowd
entries.definitionCN: 聚集；集合，由前缀 con-（共同）与 grex（群）构成

entries.definition: to keep groups apart
entries.definitionCN: 隔离；分开，由前缀 se-（分开）与 grex 构成

entries.definition: a total formed by adding things together
entries.definitionCN: 总数；集合体，由前缀 ad-（向）与 grex 构成

entries.definition: a small close group of people or things
entries.definitionCN: 一小群紧挨着的人或物；只与「聚成一群」的意思相邻，词源不同

entries.definition: willing to talk and be friendly with others
entries.definitionCN: 好交际的；友善的

entries.definition: friendly and eager to meet people
entries.definitionCN: 外向的；乐于结识他人

entries.definition: suitable for membership of clubs, and fond of their company
entries.definitionCN: 适宜入会的；爱参加社团的

entries.definition: spending time alone and avoiding company
entries.definitionCN: 独自的；喜欢独处的，与 gregarious 正相反

normalIntro.en: Gregarious keeps the Latin flock inside it: greg- is herd, and -arius means belonging to it.
normalIntro.cn: gregarious 内部藏着拉丁语里的「群」：greg- 是兽群，-arius 表示属于它。

normal.en: The root greg- means flock, and you can see it in congregate, gather into a flock.
normal.cn: 词根 greg- 意为群，在 congregate（聚成一群）里可以直接看到。

normal.en: Segregate splits the crowd apart with se-, and gregarious joins it with nothing but -arius.
normal.cn: segregate 用 se- 把人分开，gregarious 则只加 -arius 表示归属。

normal.en: A gregarious person is one who belongs to the flock by instinct, not by force.
normal.cn: gregarious 的人凭本能属于群体，而不是被勉强拉进群体。

normal.en: Sheep, wolves and elephants are gregarious animals, while leopards are solitary.
normal.cn: 羊、狼和大象是群居动物，而豹则独居。

normal.en: Gregarious is a formal word; in everyday speech people say sociable or outgoing.
normal.cn: gregarious 较正式，日常口语里多说 sociable 或 outgoing。

abstract.en: Picture one long table where every person leans towards the next to hear a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，每个人都朝旁边的人倾身去听故事。

abstract.en: Imagine a flock of birds landing on one tree until the branches bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一大群鸟一起落到同一棵树上，把枝头压弯。

abstract.en: Think of moss filling every gap in a wall until the stones look like one soft object.
abstract.cn: 想象苔藓填满墙上的每道缝隙，让石头看起来成了一整块柔软的东西。

examples.en: Gregarious by nature, he talked to everyone at the party.
examples.cn: 他天性合群，聚会上和每个人都聊了天。

examples.en: Some birds are gregarious and nest in large colonies.
examples.cn: 有些鸟很爱群居，在庞大的群落中筑巢。

examples.en: Her gregarious teammates made the new office feel welcoming.
examples.cn: 她那些爱交际的同事让新办公室显得温暖亲切。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格瑞盖瑞斯」——像「哥来盖瑞」：哥哥一来就盖在人群里，哪里热闹往哪挤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 重构词根 ger（聚集）→ 拉丁语 grex、gregis（兽群、鸟群）→ gregarius（属于群体的）→ 英语 gregarious，核心义「成群」。

sensesIntro.en: Gregarious puts the flock first, applies it to sociable people, then to animals and plants that live in groups, to the instinct behind that habit, and finally to the lively events it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: gregarious 先从「群」出发，用在爱交际的人身上，再指成群生活的动物与成簇生长的植物、这种习性背后的本能，最后指它带来的热闹场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flock pressed close together on one branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大群鸟挤在同一根枝头上。

branches.en: A person who loves company is the main sense.
branches.cn: 喜欢与人相伴的人是最主要的义项。

branches.en: Animals living in herds take the image literally again.
branches.cn: 成群生活的动物让这个意象回到字面。

branches.en: Clustered plants stretch the flock to a patch of green.
branches.cn: 成簇植物把「群」延伸到一片绿意。

branches.en: The behaviour and the instinct behind it are two views of one trait.
branches.cn: 外在行为与内在本能是同一特质的两面。

branches.en: What makes a person gregarious also makes their gatherings lively.
branches.cn: 让人合群的特性也让他们参加的聚会更加热闹。

intro.en: The Latin root greg- carries the whole idea: show, split, together and belong all hang on this flock.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 greg- 承载了整个概念：展示、拆分、相聚与归属全都挂在这只「群」上。

latinIntro.en: Latin grex, flock, and the suffix -arius, belonging to, are joined in gregarius, and its relatives are congregate, segregate and aggregate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 grex（兽群）与后缀 -arius（属于……的）合为 gregarius，同源词有 congregate、segregate、aggregate。

items.example: The root greg- opens the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 greg- 开启了整个词族。

items.example: Grex is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: grex 是形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix -arius marks belonging.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -arius 表示归属。

items.example: Gregarius is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: gregarius 是直接来源。

items.example: Gregarious narrows to the social sense.
items.exampleCN: gregarious 收窄到社交义。

items.example: The prefix con- gathers the flock.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 把群聚到一起。

items.meaning: to come together in a crowd
items.example: Congregate means to form one flock.
items.exampleCN: congregate 意为聚成一群。

items.example: The prefix se- breaks the flock apart.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 se- 把群拆开。

items.example: Segregate is the reverse image.
items.exampleCN: segregate 是反向的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms gregariousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 gregariousness。

items.meaning: the quality of being fond of company
items.example: Gregariousness names the trait.
items.exampleCN: gregariousness 指这种特质。

definition_zh: 格栅；栅栏；（地图或图表的）网格；电网；输电网；网格状规划
definition_en: a pattern of crossing lines that form squares, a frame of parallel bars, or a network such as an electricity grid
core_image: 细金属条横竖交错，织成一层带方孔的网面
scene: 老城区的街道横平竖直，在卫星图上像棋盘。From the air, the city looked like a neat grid of streets.
sceneCN: 这里 grid 是「网格」（第 2 个义项：等距横竖线交织成的方格阵）；句意：从空中看，这座城市像一张整齐的街道网格。

collocations.zh: 网格坐标；地图方格定位

derivatives.zh: 由 grid 加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成，义为「画有方格的；方格状的」
由 grid（网格）+ lock（锁住）合成，义为「交通全面堵塞；僵局」
由 grid + iron（铁）合成，义为「铁烤架；美式橄榄球场」

senses.title: A frame of bars
senses.definition: a flat frame made of parallel metal bars, used in drains, ovens, or fires
senses.definitionCN: 用平行金属条做成的扁平框子，用于排水口、烤炉或炉火中
senses.example: Leaves blocked the grid over the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 落叶堵住了排水口上的铁格栅。
senses.why: The earliest English grit or grid was a lattice of crossing bars, and a metal frame with a checker of openings is exactly that shape.
senses.whyCN: 早期英语的 grid 指横竖交锋的格状物，金属条交错、留出方形孔洞的框子正是这个形状。

senses.title: A pattern of squares
senses.definition: a pattern of straight lines crossing at right angles to form equal squares
senses.definitionCN: 直角相交的直线把平面分成相等方格所形成的图案
senses.example: The town was laid out on a grid of wide streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇按宽阔街道组成的方格网规划。
senses.why: When the bar lattice is drawn or mapped, it becomes pure lines and squares, and city planners borrow it for street plans.
senses.whyCN: 当格状框架被画到纸面或地图上时，它就变成纯粹的线和方格，城市规划者便借用它来排布街道。

senses.title: A network of power lines
senses.definition: a network of cables and substations that carries electricity from where it is made to where it is used
senses.definitionCN: 由电缆和变电站组成的网络，把电力从生产地送到使用地
senses.example: Solar farms now feed into the national grid.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳能电站如今并入国家电网供电。
senses.why: The criss-crossing squares of the streets became a metaphor for any branching net, and the electricity system is the most famous grid of all.
senses.whyCN: 街道的纵横方格被用来比喻任何分支成网的系统，而电力系统正是最有名的「网」。

senses.title: A chart layout
senses.definition: a set of faint lines on a chart or graph that helps readers read off values
senses.definitionCN: 图表上用于方便读出数值的浅色参考线
senses.example: Add a light grid to the graph so the figures are easy to read.
senses.exampleCN: 给图表加上浅色网格线，方便读出数据。
senses.why: On paper the bars become pencil lines, so any ruled chart inherits the word from the physical lattice.
senses.whyCN: 在纸上，金属条变成了铅笔线，因此任何画了参考格的图表都继承了这个词的具象来源。

senses.title: A planned road system
senses.definition: an arrangement of streets that run parallel and at right angles like a chessboard
senses.definitionCN: 街道平行排列、彼此垂直相交，形似棋盘的布局
senses.example: Drive four blocks north on the grid, then turn west.
senses.exampleCN: 沿方格路网向北开四个街区，然后向西转。
senses.why: The abstract squares of sense 02 are laid on land, so the road plan itself is called a grid.
senses.whyCN: 第 2 个义项的抽象方格被铺到地面上，道路布局本身也就叫作 grid。

senses.title: A systematic position
senses.definition: a reference position on a map marked by numbered squares
senses.definitionCN: 地图上用方格编号标示的参考位置
senses.example: The rangers gave their grid reference to the rescue team.
senses.exampleCN: 护林员把他们的网格坐标告诉了救援队。
senses.why: Once the lines have numbers, each square becomes an address, so the pattern turns into a locating tool.
senses.whyCN: 线一旦编上号，每个方格就有了地址，图案于是变成定位工具。

senses.title: An independent lifestyle
senses.definition: a way of living that does not depend on public electricity or water supplies
senses.definitionCN: 不依赖公共供电和供水的生活方式
senses.example: They built a cabin that runs off the grid all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们盖了一间整个冬天都能离网自给的小屋。
senses.why: If the grid is the public network, stepping off it means freeing yourself from the network altogether.
senses.whyCN: 如果 grid 是公共网络，那么「从网上走下来」就意味着完全摆脱这张网。

senses.title: A starting position
senses.definition: one of the marked positions from which racing cars start a race
senses.definitionCN: 赛车比赛开始前各车就位的标示位置
senses.example: He started from fifth on the grid and finished first.
senses.exampleCN: 他从第五号发车位起步，最终夺冠。
senses.why: The starting line is painted as a row of squares, so each square on the track is a grid, and by extension the whole starting order.
senses.whyCN: 起跑线被画成一排方格，赛道上每个方格就是 grid，进而指整个发车顺序。
