intro.en: Grid is first recorded in the seventeenth century as the short form of gridiron, the lattice of bars on which meat was cooked.
intro.cn: grid 首见于十七世纪，是 gridiron（烤肉用的铁格架）的缩写形式。

items.en: Gridire names the iron bars on which meat is roasted.
items.cn: gridire 指用来烤肉的铁条架。

items.en: Grid appears as a clipped form of gridiron.
items.cn: grid 作为 gridiron 的截短形式出现。

items.en: Grid also names a grating over a hole or a drain.
items.cn: grid 也指盖在坑口或排水口上的格栅。

items.en: The word spreads to any lattice of crossing lines on paper and on the land.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到纸面与地面上任何纵横交错的格网。

items.en: Grid becomes the everyday name for the electricity supply network.
items.cn: grid 成为电力供应网络的日常叫法。

items.en: Grid shifts again to computers, where a cluster of linked machines is called a grid too.
items.cn: grid 又进入计算机领域，被称为「网格计算」的一组联网机器也沿用这个词。

note.en: Grid is close to its parent gridiron and to words for grating and network, and it echoes the near-rhymes grit and grim; the origin of gridiron is uncertain, and a link with Latin cratis has been suggested but not proved.
note.cn: grid 与它的母词 gridiron 以及表示格栅、网络的词相邻，发音上又与 grit、grim 相近；gridiron 的来源不确定，有人提出与拉丁语 cratis（编成的格架）有关，但未被证实。

normalIntro.en: Grid began as a cooking rack and grew into any pattern of squares and any public network built on them.
normalIntro.cn: grid 从烤肉的铁架起步，长成任何方格图案，又长成建立在方格上的公共网络。

normal.en: Grid is a short form of gridiron, the iron bars of an oven or a grate.
normal.cn: grid 是 gridiron（炉架、炉箅）的截短形式。

normal.en: On paper, grid means the squares drawn across a map or chart.
normal.cn: 在纸面上，grid 指画在地图或图表上的方格。

normal.en: The power grid is the network that carries electricity to homes.
normal.cn: the power grid 是把电送到千家万户的网络。

normal.en: Off the grid means living without connection to public utilities.
normal.cn: off the grid 指不接入公共电网和水网地生活。

normal.en: Gridlock locks traffic in a block of streets like squares that cannot move.
normal.cn: gridlock 把车流锁在方格般的街区里，动弹不得。

abstract.en: Picture a street drain with a rusted iron lattice on top.
abstract.cn: 想象街边排水口上盖着一块生锈的铁格栅。

abstract.en: Picture a city seen from a plane, streets running in perfect squares.
abstract.cn: 想象从飞机上俯瞰城市，街道排成整齐的方格。

abstract.en: Picture hundreds of power lines fanning out over the countryside like a net.
abstract.cn: 想象几百条电线像网一样在乡野上空铺开。

examples.en: The garden was laid out on a simple grid of gravel paths.
examples.cn: 花园按简单的方格布置碎石小径。

examples.en: Storms can knock out power across the whole grid.
examples.cn: 风暴可能让整个电网停电。

examples.en: She checked the grid reference before calling the coastguard.
examples.cn: 她先核对网格坐标，才打电话给海岸警卫队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格子儿」——读音像「格」，格子、网格正是它的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: grid 是 gridiron（烤肉的铁格架）的截短形式；gridiron 本身来源不确定（一般认为与古法语有关，也有人提出联系拉丁语 cratis「编成的格架」，均未证实）。核心义为「横竖交错的格」，由铁格架扩展到纸面方格，再扩展到电网等网络。

sensesIntro.en: Grid moves from a concrete rack of iron bars to an abstract pattern of squares, then to the networks and addresses built on that pattern.
sensesIntro.cn: grid 从具象的铁格栅，走到抽象的方格图案，再走到以方格为基础的网络与坐标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: metal bars crossing into a sheet of square holes.
core.cn: 核心意象：金属条横竖相交，织成一层方孔网面。

branches.en: The physical rack of bars stays close to the oldest meaning.
branches.cn: 实物的铁条架最接近最早的词义。

branches.en: Paper, charts, and planned streets all copy the pattern of squares.
branches.cn: 纸面、图表与规划好的街道都在复制方格图案。

branches.en: A public network is a grid, and leaving it is going off the grid.
branches.cn: 公共网络也叫 grid，离开它就叫脱离电网。

branches.en: Numbered squares turn the pattern into a way of saying where you are.
branches.cn: 给方格编号，图案就变成了说明自己所在位置的方法。

branches.en: A starting square on a track comes straight from the drawn grid.
branches.cn: 赛道上的发车方格直接来自画出来的网格。

intro.en: Grid is a short English noun of uncertain origin, but it has produced a large family: gridiron, gridded, gridlock, grid reference, and the computing term grid computing.
intro.cn: grid 是来源不确定的英语短名词，但衍生出一个大家族：gridiron、gridded、gridlock、grid reference，以及计算机术语「网格计算」。

latinIntro.en: Grid has no proven Latin ancestor; a proposed link with Latin cratis, a wicker frame, remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: grid 没有已证实的拉丁语祖先；有人提出它与拉丁语 cratis（编成的格架）有关，但尚未确定。

definition_zh: 悲伤；悲痛；（因失去而）哀悼；使悲伤；使难过
definition_en: to feel or show deep sadness, especially after the death of someone you love, or to make someone feel such sadness
core_image: 一个人抱住胸口，把沉重的痛压在心口最深处
scene: 葬礼结束后的清晨，她独自坐在窗前，久久不肯说话。She still grieves for her father, two years after the funeral.
sceneCN: 这里 grieve 是「悲伤、哀悼」（第 1 个义项：因失去亲人而长期感到悲痛）；句意：葬礼过后两年，她仍在为父亲悲伤。

derivatives.zh: 由 grieve 的同源名词构成，义为「悲伤；悲痛；哀伤之事」
由 grieve 加古法语名词词尾 -ance 构成，侧重「不平；委屈；抱怨的事由」
由 grieve 加形容词词尾 -ous 构成，义为「严重的；令人痛苦的」
由 grieve 加施事词尾 -er 构成，义为「哀悼者；悲伤的人」

senses.title: To mourn a loss
senses.definition: to feel deep sadness because someone you love has died or because something precious has ended
senses.definitionCN: 因所爱的人去世或珍贵之物终结而感到深切的悲伤
senses.example: She grieved for months after her mother died.
senses.exampleCN: 母亲去世后，她悲伤了好几个月。
senses.why: The Old French verb grever means to weigh down or burden, and loss lays a heavy weight on the heart, which the English word kept as mourning.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词 grever 意为「使沉重、使负担」，而失去会把重量压在心上，英语保留了这个「沉重」的画面，用来指哀悼。

senses.title: To be deeply upset about something
senses.definition: to feel intense distress about a situation that is not about a death
senses.definitionCN: 对并非死亡的情形感到强烈的难过
senses.example: She grieved over the wasted years and the work left undone.
senses.exampleCN: 她为虚度的岁月和未完成的工作而难过。
senses.why: If any burden makes the heart heavy, then any serious misfortune, not only a death, can be grieved over.
senses.whyCN: 任何负担都会让心变沉，因此任何重大的不幸，而不仅仅是死亡，都可以成为悲伤的对象。

senses.title: To cause someone sadness
senses.definition: to make another person feel great sorrow or distress
senses.definitionCN: 使他人感到极大的悲哀或痛苦
senses.example: It grieved her to see the old school torn down.
senses.exampleCN: 看到那所老学校被拆掉，她心里很难过。
senses.why: The same heavy weight can be carried by one person and laid on someone else, so the verb also takes a direct object.
senses.whyCN: 同样的重量可以由自己承受，也可以压在别人身上，因此这个动词也能带直接宾语。

senses.title: The sad feeling itself
senses.definition: the noun use, naming deep sorrow, especially at a death
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时的含义，指深切的悲恸，尤指对死亡的反应
senses.example: Her grief was slow and quiet, and it never fully went away.
senses.exampleCN: 她的悲伤缓慢而安静，从未真正消散。
senses.why: A verb of burden naturally yields a noun of weight, and grief names the heavy thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 表示「压重」的动词自然会生出表示「重量」的名词，grief 指的就是那件沉重的东西本身。

senses.title: To complain about unfair treatment
senses.definition: an older and formal use, to raise a complaint or an official objection
senses.definitionCN: 较旧且正式的用法，指提出抱怨或正式抗议
senses.example: The farmers grieved at the new tax on their land.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们对新开征的土地税正式提出抗议。
senses.why: A burden also has a cause, and a grievance is a wrong that weighs on a person, so to grieve once meant to complain.
senses.whyCN: 沉重的负担总有其起因，grievance 就是压在身上的不公，因此 grieve 曾表示「抱怨、投诉」。

senses.title: To reprove out of duty
senses.definition: a rare and older use, to instruct or reprove someone sternly out of duty
senses.definitionCN: 少见的旧用法，指出于责任严厉地规劝或责备某人
senses.example: The elder grieved the boys for ignoring the rules of the household.
senses.exampleCN: 长辈为男孩们无视家规而责备他们。
senses.why: The Old French verb also meant to burden someone with duty, so a stern reminder of that duty was called grieving.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词也有「以责任使人负重」之义，因此把责任严厉地压回对方身上，也被称为 grieving。

senses.title: A grievance in law
senses.definition: in law and labour terms, a formal complaint about unfair treatment by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与劳动语境中，对上级不公对待的正式申诉
senses.example: The council will hear the grievance at the next meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 议会将在下次会议上听取这项申诉。
senses.why: What grieves a person can also be filed as a complaint, so the noun of weight turns into a formal procedure.
senses.whyCN: 让人悲伤的事也可以被正式提出，于是「沉重之物」这一名词又变成了一道程序。

senses.title: A view given as guidance
senses.definition: in older usage, a written opinion given to a senior as guidance or advice
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指交给上级或前辈、含指导意见的书面评点
senses.example: The clerk sent his grief on the plan to the council.
senses.exampleCN: 办事员把对该计划的书面意见交给了议事会。
senses.why: A grievance is a burden of complaint, and an older sense turned the same burden into the duty of advising a superior.
senses.whyCN: grievance 原指抱怨带来的负担，较旧的义项把这份负担转成了向上级提出建议的责任。

intro.en: Grieve comes from Old French grever, to burden or harm, from Latin gravare, to weigh down, which is built on gravis, heavy.
intro.cn: grieve 来自古法语 grever（使负重、伤害），再上溯到拉丁语 gravare（使变重），其词根是 gravis（沉重的）。

items.en: Gravis means heavy, and gravare means to load with weight.
items.cn: gravis 意为沉重，gravare 意为使负重。

items.en: A later form grevis stands behind the French branch of the word.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语的形式 grevis 位于这个词的法语支系背后。

items.en: Grever means to weigh down and also to harm or hurt.
items.cn: grever 意为使负重，也表示伤害、使痛苦。

items.en: Grieven enters English meaning to harm or oppress.
items.cn: grieven 以「伤害、压迫」之义进入英语。

items.en: The sense widens to sorrow and then to making someone sorry.
items.cn: 词义扩展到「悲伤」，继而扩展为「使人悲伤」。

items.en: Mourning at a death becomes the main sense, while grievance keeps the complaint side.
items.cn: 为死亡哀悼成为主要含义，而 grievance 保留了「抱怨」的一面。

note.en: Grieve belongs to the same heavy-root family as grave, gravity, and aggravate through Latin gravis, and it is close to mourn, lament, and sorrow.
note.cn: grieve 通过拉丁语 gravis 与 grave、gravity、aggravate 同属「沉重」词族，意义上靠近 mourn、lament 与 sorrow。

normalIntro.en: Grieve rests on Latin gravis, heavy: sorrow is a weight laid on the heart, and the whole word family keeps that weight.
normalIntro.cn: grieve 的根基是拉丁语 gravis（沉重）：悲伤就是压在心上的一块重物，整个词族都保留着这份重量。

normal.en: Grieve shares its root with grave and gravity, both about weight.
normal.cn: grieve 与 grave、gravity 同根，二者都与「重量」有关。

normal.en: Grief is the noun, and grieve is the verb: grief in the heart, grieve for the dead.
normal.cn: grief 是名词，grieve 是动词：心里有 grief，为逝者 grieve。

normal.en: Grieve for follows a person, while grieve over follows a situation.
normal.cn: grieve for 后面接人，grieve over 后面接事情。

normal.en: Grievance is a complaint: what grieves you can also be filed.
normal.cn: grievance 是申诉：让你难过的事也可以被正式提出。

normal.en: Grievous describes something that causes burdens, like a grievous error.
normal.cn: grievous 形容会造成沉重后果的事物，如 a grievous error。

abstract.en: Picture a stone being placed on a chest, one slow weight that will not lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头慢慢落到胸口，那份重量怎么也抬不起来。

abstract.en: Picture an empty room and a cup that has gone cold beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间空屋子，旁边是一杯早已凉透的茶。

abstract.en: Picture a letter that makes a reader sit down slowly and say nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信，让读它的人缓缓坐下，说不出话来。

examples.en: The whole village grieves for the family that lost their home in the flood.
examples.cn: 全村都为那个在洪水中失去家园的家庭而悲伤。

examples.en: She grieved over the letters she had never answered.
examples.cn: 她为那些从未回过的信而难过。

examples.en: It grieved him deeply that he could not attend the funeral.
examples.cn: 没能参加葬礼让他非常难过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鬼瑞夫」——心里像被鬼压住一样沉重，让人悲伤；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gravis（沉重的）→ gravare（使负重）→ 古法语 grever（使负重、伤害）→ 英语 grieve（悲伤、使人悲伤）。核心义为「压在心上的一份重量」。

sensesIntro.en: Grieve starts from the heavy weight of loss, widens to any serious misfortune, passes into the transitive sense of burdening another, and then into the nouns grief and grievance.
sensesIntro.cn: grieve 从失去带来的沉重开始，扩展到任何重大的不幸，再转为「使别人沉重」的他动用法，最后进入 grief 与 grievance 两个名词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy weight pressing on the chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块沉重的石头压在胸口。

branches.en: Mourning and grief are the two faces of one weight.
branches.cn: 哀悼与悲恸是同一份重量的两个侧面。

branches.en: Any serious misfortune can feel heavy enough to grieve.
branches.cn: 任何重大的不幸都可能沉到让人难过。

branches.en: The weight can be laid on someone else, which makes the verb transitive.
branches.cn: 这份重量可以压在别人身上，于是动词有了宾语。

branches.en: A wrong that weighs on you becomes a filed grievance.
branches.cn: 压在身上的不公，就变成可正式申诉的委屈。

branches.en: The old senses of advising and reproving carry responsibility as a burden.
branches.cn: 规劝与责备这些旧义，把责任当作一种负担。

intro.en: Grieve is built on the Latin heavy root, and its family includes grief, grievance, grievous, and griever, as well as the look-alike grave and gravity.
intro.cn: grieve 建立在拉丁语「沉重」词根上，同族词有 grief、grievance、grievous 与 griever，形近的 grave、gravity 也常与它一起记。

latinIntro.en: Latin gravis means heavy; gravare means to weigh down, and from it the French verb grever reached English as grieve.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gravis 意为沉重，gravare 意为使负重，由此而来的法语动词 grever 进入英语成为 grieve。

items.exampleCN: gravis 为整个词族提供了「重量」。

items.example: Gravare is the Latin source of the French verb.
items.exampleCN: gravare 是法语动词的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Grever carries the burden into English.
items.exampleCN: grever 把这份重量带进了英语。

definition_zh: 烤；烧烤；（用火）炙烤；烤架；（餐厅的）烤肉；严厉盘问；烤（英式拼写 grill 亦作 grille）
definition_en: to cook over direct heat on a metal frame, to question someone severely, or a metal frame or restaurant where such food is cooked
core_image: 红色的炭火上架着一层铁条，肉片在上面滋滋作响
scene: 周末傍晚，院子里升起炭火，铁网上摆满了玉米和鸡翅。They grilled corn and chicken wings over the charcoal fire.
sceneCN: 这里 grill 是「烤、炙烤」（第 1 个义项：直接在明火或铁网上烤食物）；句意：他们在炭火上烤玉米和鸡翅。

derivatives.zh: 由 grill 加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成，义为「烤过的；烤制的」
由 grill 加名词词尾 -ing 构成，义为「烤制」或「严厉的盘问」
