由 grill + work（工艺）合成，义为「格栅工艺；格栅装饰」

senses.title: To cook over direct heat
senses.definition: to cook food on a metal frame above or below strong direct heat
senses.definitionCN: 把食物放在金属网上，在强烈的直接热源之上或之下烤熟
senses.example: They grilled the fish on the hot coals.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在滚烫的炭火上烤鱼。
senses.why: Old French gril meant a grating, and the shortest step from the frame to the action is to cook on it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 gril 意为格架，从这个架子出发，最近的一步就是在它上面烤东西。

senses.title: A metal frame for cooking
senses.definition: a flat metal frame with parallel bars, used for cooking over fire
senses.definitionCN: 由平行金属条构成的扁平架子，用来在火上烹制食物
senses.example: He brushed the rusty grill before putting on the meat.
senses.exampleCN: 他先把锈了的烤架刷干净，才放上肉。
senses.why: This is the original object: the grating itself, before the verb grew out of it.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最初的本义：格架本身，动词是从它长出来的。

senses.title: To question someone severely
senses.definition: to ask someone many hard and continuous questions, especially in an official setting
senses.definitionCN: 连续向某人提出许多尖锐的问题，尤指在正式场合中
senses.example: Reporters grilled the minister for an hour about the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们就预算问题盘问了部长一个小时。
senses.why: Being grilled feels like being turned over a hot fire, so intense questioning took on the cooking image.
senses.whyCN: 被盘问就像被翻在火上烤，于是高强度的质询借用了烤肉的画面。

senses.title: A restaurant serving grilled food
senses.definition: a place or a part of a restaurant where meat and other food is cooked over fire
senses.definitionCN: 在火上烹制肉类等食物的店铺或餐厅的一个区域
senses.example: We stopped at a roadside grill for lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在路边一家烤肉店停下吃午饭。
senses.why: A place named after its equipment is common, so the frame gave its name to the shop that uses it.
senses.whyCN: 以设备命名场所很常见，于是这个架子把名字给了使用它的店铺。

senses.title: Heat coming from above
senses.definition: a way of cooking in which the heat sits above the food, as in an oven top element
senses.definitionCN: 热源位于食物上方的一种烹调方式，如烤箱顶部的发热元件
senses.example: Switch the oven to grill to brown the top of the pie.
senses.exampleCN: 把烤箱调到上火烤，将派皮表面烤成金黄色。
senses.why: The oven copied the outdoor frame, but now the bars sit above the food, so grill also names top heat.
senses.whyCN: 烤箱模仿了户外的烤架，只是铁条现在位于食物上方，因此 grill 也指来自上方的烤热。

senses.title: A strong public pressure
senses.definition: sustained and harsh criticism or pressure put on a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 对个人或团体持续而猛烈的批评或压力
senses.example: The company faced a two-week grill from the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司遭到媒体连续两周的猛烈抨击。
senses.why: Verbal heat is still heat, so a long public attack is imagined as cooking someone slowly.
senses.whyCN: 言语的热度也是热度，于是长时间的舆论围攻被想象成慢慢把人烤熟。

senses.title: A decorative grille
senses.definition: an open metalwork of bars used on a car front, a window, or a building
senses.definitionCN: 装在汽车前部、窗户或建筑上的开放式金属条制品
senses.example: A silver grill stood out on the front of the old car.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆老爷车的前脸有一道醒目的银色格栅。
senses.why: The same full form is written grille for protection or ornament, so any lattice of bars joins the family.
senses.whyCN: 保护或装饰用途的同形词常写作 grille，于是任何铁条格网都属于这个词族。

senses.title: A dish of grilled food
senses.definition: a meal of meat or vegetables that has been grilled, often served in a restaurant
senses.definitionCN: 烤制的肉类或蔬菜菜式，常在餐厅供应
senses.example: She ordered a mixed grill with chips and salad.
senses.exampleCN: 她点了一份什锦烤肉，配薯条和沙拉。
senses.why: The verb turned into a countable noun for the finished dish, and then into a menu word.
senses.whyCN: 动词随即可数化为「烤好的一盘菜」，进而成为菜单上的词。

intro.en: Grill comes through French from Latin craticula, a small grating, from cratis, a wicker or lattice frame.
intro.cn: grill 经法语来自拉丁语 craticula（小格架），而其词根是 cratis（编成的格架）。

items.en: Cratis means a wickerwork or a lattice of crossed pieces.
items.cn: cratis 意为编结格架或交叉而成的格状物。

items.en: Craticula, a small cratis, names the little grating of a cooking fire.
items.cn: craticula（cratis 的小称）指灶火上的小格架。

items.en: Gril names a grating and griller means to cook on it.
items.cn: gril 指格架，griller 意为在格架上烤。

items.en: Grill enters English first as the frame for cooking.
items.cn: grill 先以「烤架」之义进入英语。

items.en: The verb spreads to any cooking over open heat.
items.cn: 动词义扩展到任何在明火上烹制的方式。

items.en: Grill widens to restaurants, to top-heat ovens, and to harsh questioning.
items.cn: grill 扩展到烤肉店、上火烤的烤箱，以及严厉盘问。

note.en: Grill is close to grille, its sister spelling for decorative lattice, to grid and gridiron, and to the cooking words roast, barbecue, and broil, plus the questioning verb interrogate.
note.cn: grill 与装饰性格栅的姊妹拼写 grille、与 grid、gridiron 相邻，烹调义上靠近 roast、barbecue、broil，盘问义上靠近 interrogate。

entries.definition: an ornamental metal lattice
entries.definitionCN: 装饰性金属格栅。与 grill 同源，多用于装饰与防护

entries.definition: a frame of bars or a pattern of squares
entries.definitionCN: 格栅或方格网。只是拼写与含义相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an iron frame for grilling
entries.definitionCN: 铁烤架。只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to cook in an oven or over a fire
entries.definitionCN: 烘烤；烤制

entries.definition: to cook food outdoors on a rack over an open fire
entries.definitionCN: 在户外明火上烧烤

entries.definition: to question someone thoroughly
entries.definitionCN: 审问；质问

normalIntro.en: Grill begins with a metal frame, then becomes the fire, then the place, then the pressure of hard questioning.
normalIntro.cn: grill 从一层金属格架开始，接着变成火、变成场所，最后变成严词质问所带来的压力。

normal.en: Grill shares a Latin root with grille, both from the lattice cratis.
normal.cn: grill 与 grille 同源，都来自表示格架的 cratis。

normal.en: To grill food is to cook it right over the heat, not in a pot.
normal.cn: grill 食物就是直接在火上方烤，而不是用锅煮。

normal.en: A mixed grill is a plate of several grilled meats.
normal.cn: a mixed grill 是一盘什锦烤肉。

normal.en: To grill a person is to question them the way fire heats food.
normal.cn: grill 某人，就是像用火烤食物那样连续问他问题。

normal.en: Grilled and grilling keep the -ll- spelling, never -led with a single l.
normal.cn: grilled、grilling 都保留双写 l，不写成单 l 的形式。

abstract.en: Picture fat dripping onto red coals and hissing into smoke.
abstract.cn: 想象油脂滴到通红的炭上，滋一声冒出烟。

abstract.en: Picture a black iron rack with bars like the rungs of a ladder.
abstract.cn: 想象一层黑色铁网，铁条像梯子的横档。

abstract.en: Picture a small room where a witness sits under a single hot lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小屋子，证人在一盏烤人的灯下坐着。

examples.en: She grilled peppers and aubergines on the garden grill.
examples.cn: 她在院子里的烤架上烤了甜椒和茄子。

examples.en: After the match, the coach was grilled about the late substitution.
examples.cn: 比赛结束后，教练被反复追问那次迟来的换人。

examples.en: The fish is best grilled quickly so it stays moist.
examples.cn: 这种鱼最好快速烤制，才能保持鲜嫩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格瑞尔」——先想到「格子」，铁架上的格子烤东西，就是烤；被架在火上连珠炮问，就是盘问。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 cratis（编成的格架）→ craticula（小格架）→ 古法语 gril / griller → 英语 grill。核心义为「铁条格架」，再由架子引申出「在架上烤」「烤肉店」与比喻义「把人架在火上盘问」。

sensesIntro.en: Grill starts from the iron frame, turns the frame into a cooking action, then into a place, a top-heat oven setting and a dish, and finally reapplies the cooking heat to the experience of being questioned.
sensesIntro.cn: grill 从铁格架出发，把架子变成烤的动作，再变成场所、上火烤的设置和一盘菜，最后把烤肉的热度转用到被追问的体验上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bars of iron over a bed of glowing coals.
core.cn: 核心意象：红通通的炭火上方架着铁条。

branches.en: The frame and the act of cooking on it are the two oldest senses.
branches.cn: 铁架与在架上烤，是最早的两个义项。

branches.en: Verbal heat becomes severe questioning and public attack.
branches.cn: 言语的热度变成严厉盘问与舆论围攻。

branches.en: Where grilled food is served and the dish itself both take the name.
branches.cn: 供应烤肉的地方和那盘菜本身都沿用这个词。

branches.en: Heat from below and heat from above are two versions of one grill.
branches.cn: 来自下方和上方的热，是同一种烧烤的两个版本。

branches.en: Cooking bars and decorative bars are the same lattice in two jobs.
branches.cn: 烤架的铁条与装饰铁条，是同一个格架的两种用途。

intro.en: Grill is a Latin lattice word in English dress, and its family runs from the action (grilled, grilling) to compounds such as grillroom and grillwork.
intro.cn: grill 是一颗披上英语外衣的拉丁「格架」词，词族从动作义（grilled、grilling）延伸到 grillroom、grillwork 这类合成词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cratis means a wicker or lattice frame, and its small form craticula gives the French and English names for a cooking rack.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cratis 意为编成的格架，其小称 craticula 则给出了法语和英语中「烤架」的名称。

items.example: Cratis gives the lattice image.
items.exampleCN: cratis 提供了格架的意象。

items.example: Craticula is the small cooking frame.
items.exampleCN: craticula 指烹调用的小格架。

items.example: Gril is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: gril 是直接的法语来源。

items.meaning: a frame, to cook on it
items.example: They cook on a grill at weekends.
items.exampleCN: 他们周末用烤架做饭。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms grilled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 grilled。

items.example: We had grilled vegetables.
items.exampleCN: 我们吃了烤蔬菜。

items.meaningCN: 行为或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms grilling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 grilling。

items.example: He did not enjoy the grilling.
items.exampleCN: 他并不喜欢那场盘问。

items.example: A grille hides the car radiator.
items.exampleCN: 一道格栅遮住了汽车散热器。

items.example: We ate at an old grillroom.
items.exampleCN: 我们在一家老式烤肉餐厅吃饭。

items.example: The suffix -work forms grillwork.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -work 构成 grillwork。

items.example: The balcony has fine grillwork.
items.exampleCN: 阳台上有精致的格栅装饰。

definition_zh: 严酷的；无情的；严峻的；阴森的；令人不快的；坚毅的
definition_en: very serious and harsh, with no sign of comfort, humour, or hope
core_image: 一张紧绷的脸：眉毛压低、嘴角下撇、眼神里没有笑
scene: 病房的门刚打开，医生把家属叫到走廊，压低了声音。The doctor gave a grim shake of the head and asked the whole family to sit down.
sceneCN: 这里 grim 是「严峻的、令人心沉的」（第 2 个义项：形容局面坏得没有回旋余地）；句意：医生脸色严峻地摇了摇头，请全家人都坐下。

pos.zh: 严酷的；无情的；严峻的；阴森的；令人不快的；坚定的

collocations.zh: 坏消息；令人沮丧的消息
死神（扛着镰刀的骷髅形象）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「严峻地；阴森地；坚决地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「严酷；阴森；坚毅」
词形相似但词源不同（一般认为源自法语），义为「鬼脸；做鬼脸」
由 grim 与 faced 复合而成，义为「面容阴沉的」

senses.title: Fierce and merciless
senses.definition: fierce, cruel, and showing no mercy
senses.definitionCN: 凶猛的、残忍的，毫不留情
senses.example: The grim truth is that no one searched for the lost children.
senses.exampleCN: 严酷的真相是：没有人去寻找那些走失的孩子。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word describes something savage and fierce, and a face without softness keeps that same hardness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层指凶恶、凶猛的事物，而一张没有柔和感的脸正是保留了同样的「硬」，所以「严酷」是这个核心意象最直接的长出。

senses.title: Bleak and without hope
senses.definition: used of a situation that is very bad and seems to offer no hope
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容局面极坏、看不到希望
senses.example: The rescue team painted a grim picture of the floods.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队对洪水的情况描绘得很严峻。
senses.why: When the face sets hard because there is nothing to smile about, the word moves from the face to the situation that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 当一张脸因为没什么可笑而绷紧时，这个词就从脸挪到了造成这张脸的局面：局面本身严峻、无望。

senses.title: Gloomy and forbidding in appearance
senses.definition: looking dark, cold, and unpleasant, so that it makes people uneasy
senses.definitionCN: 看上去阴暗、冷硬、令人不安
senses.example: A grim ruin of a house stood at the end of the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 小巷尽头立着一座阴森的废屋。
senses.why: The grim face is an image anyone can read, so it is easily projected onto buildings, skies, and rooms that look equally hard and joyless.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的脸人人都读得懂，于是很容易被投射到同样冷硬、毫无喜气的建筑、天空和房间里，形成「阴森」之义。

senses.title: Very unpleasant or shocking
senses.definition: very unpleasant, shocking, or frightening, especially in an everyday situation
senses.definitionCN: 非常令人不快、震惊或恐惧，尤见于日常情境
senses.example: It was a grim moment when the lights went out in the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 医院里突然停电的那一刻令人心惊。
senses.why: From the harsh face comes a general label for anything that feels hard to face, including bad news, accidents, and scary scenes.
senses.whyCN: 从那张冷酷的脸出发，凡是让人觉得「难以面对」的事物都可以用这个词标记：坏消息、事故、可怕的场面，于是产生了「令人不快、可怕」的义项。

senses.title: Determined in spite of hardship
senses.definition: showing a quiet, humourless determination to keep going through difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 表现出不动声色、不靠玩笑支撑的坚持
senses.example: She set off for work each day with grim determination.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天带着咬牙的决心去上班。
senses.why: A face set tight can also signal resolve rather than anger, so grim can mark an effort that will not soften or give up.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的脸既可以表示愤怒，也可以表示决心，所以 grim 也能形容那种不肯软化、不肯放弃的努力，「咬牙坚持」便由此而来。

intro.en: Grim is an Old English word for what is fierce, harsh, or savage, with a clear home in Germanic languages.
intro.cn: grim 是古英语中表示「凶猛、严酷、野蛮」的词，在日耳曼语族中有清楚的同源对应。

items.en: The reconstructed form grimmo means fierce or grim.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式 grimmo 意为凶猛、冷酷。

items.en: Grim is recorded in Old English with the sense fierce, cruel, or stern.
items.cn: 古英语中的 grim 已见记录，意为凶猛的、残忍的、严厉的。

items.en: Old Norse grimmr shares the same family and confirms the meaning.
items.cn: 古北欧语 grimmr 属于同一词族，印证了这层含义。

items.en: Grim widens to describe a harsh-looking face and a fierce appearance.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，grim 扩展到形容严厉的面孔和凶恶的外表。

items.en: Writers extend grim to bleak places and hopeless situations.
items.cn: 到十八世纪前后，作家把它延伸到阴沉的场所与无望的局面。

items.en: The word now covers bad news, grim determination, and the grim reaper.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它涵盖坏消息、咬牙的决心以及「死神」的固定形象。

note.en: Grim is a hard-faced word, close to grimace and grimy in form and to severe, bleak, and ghastly in meaning.
note.cn: grim 是「脸很硬」的词，形式上与 grimace、grimy 相近，意义上与 severe、bleak、ghastly 相邻。

entries.definition: a twisted expression of pain or disgust
entries.definitionCN: 因痛苦或厌恶而扭曲的表情；这个词只是开头几个字母与 grim 相同，一般认为来自法语，词源不同。

entries.definition: covered with dirt or soot
entries.definitionCN: 满是污垢的；它只是拼写从 grim 岔出一截，词根来自表示油污的词，词源不同。

entries.definition: in a serious, harsh, or determined way
entries.definitionCN: 严峻地；坚决地，由 grim 加副词后缀构成。

entries.definition: very harsh and strict
entries.definitionCN: 严厉的；苛刻的，更侧重规矩与惩戒，而不在神情。

entries.definition: cold, empty, and offering no hope
entries.definitionCN: 阴冷的；荒凉的；无望的，更强调空荡与没有出路。

entries.definition: silent, unfriendly, and unsmiling
entries.definitionCN: 阴沉寡言的；脸色难看的，更侧重性格上的不亲和。

normalIntro.en: Grim is not a long story: it has meant fierce and harsh since Old English, and every modern sense still shows a hard face.
normalIntro.cn: grim 的来路并不复杂：古英语里就表示凶猛、严酷，现代各个义项都还带着那张硬邦邦的脸。

normal.en: Grim is an Old English word with no Latin behind it, so treat the g-r-i-m letters as one solid block.
normal.cn: grim 是古英语词，背后没有拉丁语，把这五个字母当成一个整体来记。

normal.en: The adverb grimly and the noun grimness are simply grim plus -ly and -ness.
normal.cn: 副词 grimly 和名词 grimness 就是 grim 分别加上 -ly 与 -ness。

normal.en: The reaper who carries a scythe is fixed in English as the grim reaper.
normal.cn: 扛着镰刀的死神在英语里固定叫 the grim reaper。

normal.en: Grim determination is a set phrase for a stubborn effort that will not soften.
normal.cn: grim determination 是固定说法，指不肯松口的顽强努力。

normal.en: Do not confuse grim with grimy: one is a hard face, the other is dirty hands.
normal.cn: 不要混淆 grim 与 grimy：前者是硬邦邦的脸，后者是脏兮兮的手。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow, tight mouth and heavy brows with no smile anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一张紧抿的薄嘴和压低的眉毛，全无笑意。

abstract.en: Imagine a wall without a window, no light getting through.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵没有窗的墙，透不进一点光。

abstract.en: See a ruined house in fog, its door hanging open.
abstract.cn: 想象雾里一座废屋，门歪着敞开。

examples.en: The news from the coast was grim.
examples.cn: 来自海岸的消息令人沮丧。

examples.en: He looked grim as he read the letter.
examples.cn: 他读那封信时脸色阴沉。

examples.en: Years of grim determination finally paid off.
examples.cn: 多年的咬牙坚持终于有了回报。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 grim 想成「格姆」——一位长相凶、脸色铁青的巨人，谁看见都发怵；这只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 古英语 grim（凶猛、残酷、严厉），同源于古北欧语 grimmr 及重构的原始日耳曼语 grimmo，核心义「硬、凶、无情」，词根并非来自拉丁语。

sensesIntro.en: Grim begins on the face that cannot soften, then spreads to bleak situations, forbidding places, shocking moments, and stubborn resolve.
sensesIntro.cn: grim 从一张硬到放松不下来的脸出发，再扩散到无望的局面、阴森的场所、令人心惊的时刻和咬牙的坚持。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard-set face with no hint of a smile.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张绷得紧紧、毫无笑意的脸。

branches.en: The oldest layer is simple fierceness and lack of mercy.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层就是单纯的凶猛与无情。

branches.en: A face with nothing to smile about points to a bleak, hopeless situation.
branches.cn: 一张没什么可笑的脸，指向无望、严峻的局面。

branches.en: The same hardness belongs to dark houses, cold skies, and gloomy rooms.
branches.cn: 同样的冷硬也属于阴暗的房子、寒冷的天空和阴沉的房间。

branches.en: Anything hard to face, from bad news to a blackout, earns the label.
branches.cn: 任何让人难以面对的事，从坏消息到停电，都可以用这个词。

branches.en: The set jaw shows both harshness and a resolve that will not bend.
branches.cn: 咬紧的下巴既显得严酷，也显出不肯弯折的决心。

intro.en: Grim is a native Germanic adjective, so the forms built on it are English suffixes rather than Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: grim 是本土的日耳曼语形容词，围绕它构成的都是英语后缀，而非拉丁语前缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is known for grim; the closest relatives are Germanic, as Old Norse shows, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: grim 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，最近的同源词都属于日耳曼语族，古北欧语可以佐证，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Grim is the base form used all year round.
items.exampleCN: grim 是最基础的形式，可用于各种语境。

items.example: The double consonant keeps the m short.
items.exampleCN: 双写辅音是为了保持短元音。

items.example: Grimmest is used for the worst extreme.
items.exampleCN: grimmest 用于最极端的程度。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns grim into grimly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 grim 变成 grimly。

items.example: The crew grimly carried on in the storm.
items.exampleCN: 船员们在风暴中咬牙坚持。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms grimness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 grimness。

items.example: The grimness of the winter was hard to forget.
items.exampleCN: 那个冬天的严酷让人难以忘记。

items.example: Grim-faced staff cleared the square.
items.exampleCN: 面色阴沉的工作人员清空了广场。

items.example: Grimace looks similar but comes from a different root.
items.exampleCN: grimace 看起来相似，但词源不同。

definition_zh: 满是污垢的；积满油污的；肮脏的；不光彩的
definition_en: covered with a layer of dirt, soot, or oily filth that has built up over time
core_image: 手指在窗户上抹过，留下一道灰黑的印子
scene: 工人从车间出来，指甲缝里嵌着黑泥，袖口被机油蹭得发亮。He wiped his grimy hands on his overalls and sat down to eat.
sceneCN: 这里 grimy 是「满是污垢的」（第 1 个义项：表面覆着一层日积月累的脏东西）；句意：他在工装裤上擦了擦脏兮兮的手，坐下来吃饭。

pos.zh: 满是污垢的；积满油污的；肮脏的；不光彩的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「污垢、油垢」，也可作动词表示「使沾上污垢」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「污秽；肮脏」
常见短语，义为「覆满灰尘的」

senses.title: Covered with built-up dirt
senses.definition: covered with a layer of dirt or grease that has gathered over time
senses.definitionCN: 表面覆盖着一层长期积累的灰尘或油污
senses.example: The kitchen window was too grimy to see through.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的窗户太脏，根本透不进光。
senses.why: The base noun means the dirt layer itself, and the ending -y means full of it, so a grimy thing is one holding all that collected dirt.
senses.whyCN: 基础名词指的就是那层污垢本身，词尾 -y 表示「满是……」，所以 grimy 就是「积着那一层层脏东西」的东西。

senses.title: Filthy because of work or soot
senses.definition: made dirty especially by soot, smoke, or heavy manual work
senses.definitionCN: 尤指因煤烟、烟气或繁重体力劳动而变脏
senses.example: The miners came up into the sunlight with grimy faces.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工们一脸煤灰地来到阳光下。
senses.why: Where there is smoke and hard labour, the dirt settles faster, so the word is at home with miners, kitchens, and old factories.
senses.whyCN: 有烟和重活的地方，脏东西落得更快，所以这个词总跟矿工、厨房和老工厂连在一起。

senses.title: Sordid in a moral sense
senses.definition: used figuratively of something mean, secret, or morally dirty
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指卑劣、隐秘或在道德上肮脏的事
senses.example: The reporter uncovered the grimy details of the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 记者挖出了那笔交易里见不得人的细节。
senses.why: If a surface can hold dirt, a story can hold shame, so the everyday stain easily becomes a moral stain.
senses.whyCN: 表面能积灰，事情也能积丑，于是日常的「污渍」很自然地变成了道德上的污点。

intro.en: Grimy is formed from the noun grime and the adjective ending -y, and grime itself is a word of uncertain origin recorded in Middle English.
intro.cn: grimy 由名词 grime 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，而 grime 本身来源不确定，早在中古英语中就有记录。

items.en: Grime is first recorded in Middle English, meaning dirt or smut.
items.cn: grime 首见于中古英语，意为污垢、烟灰。

items.en: Several Germanic and Dutch parallels are proposed, but no origin is certain.
items.cn: 关于它是否与日耳曼语或荷兰语的某些词同源，学界有若干推测，但确切来源不确定。

items.en: The adjective grimy appears, built from grime plus the ending -y.
items.cn: 由 grime 加词尾 -y 构成的形容词 grimy 出现。

items.en: Grimy is used of windows, hands, and streets in industrial towns.
items.cn: 在工业城镇里，grimy 被用来形容窗户、双手和街道。

items.en: The word also takes a figurative sense for sordid affairs.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词也发展出形容卑劣勾当的比喻义。

note.en: Grimy is the everyday word for dirt that has settled in, close to the noun grime, to its look-alike grim, and to dirty and filthy.
note.cn: grimy 是形容「积着脏东西」的日常词，与名词 grime 同根，与外形相近的 grim 容易混，与 dirty、filthy 意义相邻。

entries.definition: a layer of dirt, especially on a surface
entries.definitionCN: （尤指表面上）积起的污垢；是 grimy 的基础名词。

entries.definition: harsh, gloomy, or determined
entries.definitionCN: 严酷的；阴森的；这词只是与 grimy 开头几个字母相似，词源不同（grim 来自古英语）。

entries.definition: the state of being dirty and grimy
entries.definitionCN: 污秽；肮脏的状态，由 grimy 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: not clean
entries.definitionCN: 脏的；不干净的，是最普通、覆盖最广的说法。

entries.definition: covered with black soot
entries.definitionCN: 被黑色煤烟灰覆盖的，只针对烟灰这一种污垢。

entries.definition: extremely dirty and unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 极其肮脏、令人恶心的，语气比 grimy 重得多。

normalIntro.en: Strip off the last letter and you find grime, so grimy simply means full of grime, the settled dirt that will not wipe off in one go.
normalIntro.cn: 去掉最后一个字母就露出 grime，所以 grimy 就是「满是 grime」，那种一下子擦不净的积垢。

normal.en: Grime plus the ending -y gives the adjective grimy, exactly as frost gives frosty.
normal.cn: grime 加词尾 -y 就是形容词 grimy，就像 frost 加 -y 得 frosty。

normal.en: The noun form griminess is made with the familiar ending -ness.
normal.cn: 名词形式 griminess 由常见的 -ness 构成。

normal.en: Keep the e before the ending: grime becomes grimy with no missing letters, only a swap.
normal.cn: 词尾前保持字母顺序：grime 变 grimy 时一个字母都不丢，只是换了结尾。

normal.en: Natural partners are grimy hands, grimy windows, and grimy walls.
normal.cn: 自然搭配是 grimy hands、grimy windows、grimy walls。

normal.en: Do not mix it up with grim: a grim face is stern, a grimy face is black with soot.
normal.cn: 别和 grim 混：grim 的脸是严厉，grimy 的脸是被煤灰糊黑了。

abstract.en: See a fingertip drawn across a window and a grey streak left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指划过窗玻璃，留下一道灰印。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen wall above a stove after a year of cooking.
abstract.cn: 想象一口锅前那面墙，做饭做了一年后变成什么样子。

abstract.en: Imagine a stolen file with a smudge on every page.
abstract.cn: 想象一份见不得光的文件，每一页都带着污点。

examples.en: The cups were grimy from years of use.
examples.cn: 这些杯子因为用了多年而污迹斑斑。

examples.en: He wiped the grimy windscreen with his sleeve.
examples.cn: 他用袖子擦了擦脏兮兮的挡风玻璃。

examples.en: The team walked down a grimy narrow street.
examples.cn: 队伍沿着一条肮脏狭窄的街道走着。

dict_mnemonic.text: grimy 的后半截读起来像「米」——一袋米放久了落满灰，抓一把都沾手；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: grime（污垢、油垢，中古英语已见记录，来源不确定）+ 形容词词尾 -y（满是……的）→ grimy，核心义「表面覆着一层积垢」。

sensesIntro.en: Grimy starts with physical dirt on a surface, narrows to soot and sweat from heavy work, and then extends to dirty dealings.
sensesIntro.cn: grimy 先指物体表面上实打实的污垢，再缩小到重活留下的烟灰与汗渍，最后延伸到见不得人的勾当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey smear left by a finger on a window.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指在窗上抹出的一道灰印。

branches.en: A surface coated with settled dirt is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 覆着积垢的表面是这个词最朴素的义项。

branches.en: Soot, smoke, and heavy work make the dirt darker and stickier.
branches.cn: 烟灰、煤烟和重活让污垢更黑、更黏。

branches.en: A stain on a surface turns into a stain on a story.
branches.cn: 表面的污渍转化为事件上的污点。

branches.en: Both senses describe dirt that has had time to build up.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述经过时间积累起来的脏。

branches.en: Hard, shadowy work and shady dealings share the same dark coating.
branches.cn: 辛苦隐蔽的劳动与见不得人的交易共用同一层黑漆漆的外衣。

intro.en: Grimy is built from the noun grime and a single familiar English ending, with a few compounds and derived forms around it.
intro.cn: grimy 由名词 grime 加一个常见英语词尾构成，周围还有若干复合形式与派生形式。

latinIntro.en: Grime has no reliable Latin source, so the Latin side is left empty and the word is explained through its English parts.
latinIntro.cn: grime 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空，改从句法构词角度解释。

items.example: The grime on the tiles was hard to remove.
items.exampleCN: 瓷砖上的积垢很难去掉。

items.example: The suffix -y turns grime into grimy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 grime 变成 grimy。

items.example: The grimy doorknob had not been cleaned for years.
items.exampleCN: 那个脏兮兮的门把手好几年没擦过。

items.example: The back stairs were grimier than the front hall.
items.exampleCN: 后楼梯比前厅更脏。

items.example: That cellar corner was the grimiest place in the house.
items.exampleCN: 地下室那个角落是整间屋子里最脏的地方。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms griminess.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 griminess。

items.example: The griminess of the workshop stained every shirt.
items.exampleCN: 车间的脏污把每件衬衫都弄花了。

items.example: The grime-covered sign was barely readable.
items.exampleCN: 那块覆满污垢的牌子几乎看不清了。

items.example: A strong spray can degrease a grimy stove.
items.exampleCN: 强力清洁剂能去掉油污灶台上的污渍。

definition_zh: 咧嘴笑；露齿而笑；龇牙咧嘴；苦笑；咧嘴笑的样子
definition_en: to smile widely so that the teeth show
core_image: 一张咧开的大嘴：嘴角向两边扯开，露出一排牙
scene: 孩子拿到新自行车的第一天，绕着院子骑了一圈又一圈。He jumped off and grinned at his grandfather, showing the gap where a tooth had gone.
sceneCN: 这里 grin 是「咧嘴笑」（第 1 个义项：张大嘴露出牙齿的笑）；句意：他跳下车，朝爷爷咧嘴一笑，露出缺了颗牙的空当。

pos.zh: 咧嘴笑；露齿而笑；龇牙咧嘴

collocations.phrase: wipe the grin off your face
collocations.zh: 收起笑脸（常含责备口气）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「咧嘴笑的；咧嘴笑」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「爱咧嘴笑的人」
形容词加 -ly 构成（较少见），义为「咧嘴笑着地」

senses.title: To smile widely showing the teeth
senses.definition: to smile with the mouth open wide so that the teeth show
senses.definitionCN: 张大嘴笑，露出牙齿
senses.example: She grinned when she saw the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她看到蛋糕时咧嘴笑了。
senses.why: The oldest English use of the word points at showing the teeth, and that bare-toothed mouth is exactly what the core image draws.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早在英语里就指「露出牙齿」，而这张露着牙的嘴正是核心意象所画的画面，所以「露齿而笑」是最直接的长出。

senses.title: To smile without real joy
senses.definition: to smile in a fixed or strained way when you feel no real pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 在没有真正喜悦时，摆出僵硬或勉强做出的笑容
senses.example: He grinned and said the pay cut was fine by him.
senses.exampleCN: 他苦笑着说，降薪他没意见。
senses.why: The same wide mouth can hide pain as easily as it shows joy, so the bare-toothed grin turns into a mask pulled over bad news.
senses.whyCN: 同样咧开的大嘴既能露出喜悦，也能掩住难受，于是「露齿的笑」就变成盖在坏消息上的面具，由此有了「苦笑」。

senses.title: To draw the lips back in anger
senses.definition: of an animal or an angry person, to pull the lips back from the teeth as a warning
senses.definitionCN: 动物或发怒的人把嘴唇向后拉、露出牙齿以示威胁
senses.example: The dog grinned at the postman through the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗隔着大门朝邮递员龇牙。
senses.why: For dogs and wolves, bared teeth are a threat, so the very same mouth movement that means welcome in people means danger in animals.
senses.whyCN: 对狗和狼来说，露出的牙是警告，所以同一个张嘴动作：在人身上是欢迎，在动物身上就成了危险。

senses.title: A broad smile
senses.definition: a broad smile in which the teeth show
senses.definitionCN: 露出牙齿的大笑
senses.example: The boy came in with a big grin on his face.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩一脸大笑着走进来。
senses.why: The verb easily becomes a noun because what people remember is the visible shape of the mouth, which can be named as a thing.
senses.whyCN: 动词很容易转成名词，因为人们记住的是那张嘴的可见形状，形状本身就可以当成一样东西来称呼。

intro.en: Grin is an Old English verb for drawing back the lips and showing the teeth, and its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: grin 是古英语动词，表示把嘴唇向后拉、露出牙齿；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Grennian or grennian first means to snarl and show the teeth.
items.cn: 古英语 grennian（常写作 grennian 等变体）最初意为龇牙怒吼、露齿。

items.en: The form settles on grin, still close to baring the teeth.
items.cn: 中古英语中词形定型为 grin，仍侧重「露出牙齿」。

items.en: No certain relation to Latin or Greek has been shown for the deeper root.
items.cn: 一般认为，它更深的词根没有可靠的拉丁语或希腊语对应。

items.en: Grin begins to mean a friendly or foolish wide smile.
items.cn: 十六世纪前后，grin 开始表示友好或傻气的咧嘴大笑。

items.en: The idiom grin and bear it is recorded in the modern sense.
items.cn: 短语 grin and bear it 以现代含义见于记录。

items.en: Both the smiling and the snarling senses survive, along with the noun.
items.cn: 「笑」与「龇牙」两种含义都保留下来，名词用法也随之通行。

note.en: Grin is the broad, bare-toothed smile, close in form to grind and grim and in meaning to smile, smirk, and beam.
note.cn: grin 是张嘴露牙的大笑，形式上易与 grind、grim 混，意义上与 smile、smirk、beam 相邻。

entries.definition: to crush into powder or rub harshly
entries.definitionCN: 磨碎；摩擦挤压；与 grin 只差一个字母，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: harsh and unsmiling
entries.definitionCN: 严酷的；阴沉的；与 grin 拼写相近而意思近乎相反，词源不同。

entries.definition: smiling widely with teeth showing
entries.definitionCN: 咧嘴笑的，由 grin 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: to turn up the corners of the mouth
entries.definitionCN: 微笑，嘴可以不张、牙可以不露，比 grin 幅度小。

entries.definition: to smile with great happiness
entries.definitionCN: 喜气洋洋地笑，重点在满心的喜悦而不在露牙。

entries.definition: to smile in a smug or silly way
entries.definitionCN: 得意地或傻气地笑，带有不该笑的自得意味。

normalIntro.en: Grin carries an old idea of bared teeth, which is why the mouth is always wide open in every sense from joy to warning.
normalIntro.cn: grin 保留着「露出牙齿」的古老意味，所以无论是开心还是警告，它的嘴永远张得很大。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the n: grinned, and the same doubling appears in grinning.
normal.cn: 过去式要把 n 双写：grinned，ing 形式同样是 grinning。

normal.en: A familiar idiom is grin and bear it, meaning to endure without complaining.
normal.cn: 常见短语是 grin and bear it，意思是咬牙忍着、不抱怨。

normal.en: Grin from ear to ear describes a smile that takes up the whole face.
normal.cn: grin from ear to ear 形容笑得整个脸都咧开。

normal.en: The noun grin usually takes a or the: a big grin, the grin on her face.
normal.cn: 名词 grin 前通常加 a 或 the：a big grin、the grin on her face。

normal.en: Compare smirk: smirk adds smugness, grin alone is just the wide mouth.
normal.cn: 对比 smirk：smirk 多了自得的味道，grin 本身只是那张大开的嘴。

abstract.en: Picture a child holding up a drawing, teeth on full display.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子举着自己画的画，笑得满口牙都露出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a person nodding at bad news with the mouth still stretched wide.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人听到坏消息时点头，嘴却还咧得很开。

abstract.en: See a dog behind a fence pulling back its lips at a stranger.
abstract.cn: 想象篱笆后的一条狗朝陌生人把嘴唇往上一掀。

examples.en: She grinned at me across the busy street.
examples.cn: 她隔着繁忙的街道朝我咧嘴笑。

examples.en: He answered with a sheepish grin.
examples.cn: 他不好意思地咧嘴一笑，算是回答。

examples.en: The idea made him grin from ear to ear.
examples.cn: 这个想法让他笑得合不拢嘴。

dict_mnemonic.text: grin 读起来像「格林」——格林童话里的小家伙一高兴就咧开大嘴，牙齿全露出来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 grennian（龇牙、露齿而笑，词形有多种变体）→ 中古英语 grin，核心义「把嘴唇拉开、露出牙齿」，更深的词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Grin moves from the wide, bare-toothed smile, to a smile used to cover pain, to the bared teeth of an angry animal, and finally to the smile as a thing you can see.
sensesIntro.cn: grin 从张着嘴露牙的笑出发，转而指掩盖难受的苦笑、动物发怒时的龇牙，最后成为可以看见的「那个笑」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mouth pulled wide with a row of teeth showing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张咧开的嘴，露出一排牙。

branches.en: The simple, happy wide smile is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 简单而愉快的咧嘴大笑是日常义项。

branches.en: The same stretched mouth can be worn to hide discomfort.
branches.cn: 同样咧开的嘴也可以用来掩盖不安。

branches.en: Bared teeth in animals turn the gesture into a threat.
branches.cn: 动物露齿时，同一个动作就变成威胁。

branches.en: The smile can be seen as an object, so the verb gives a noun.
branches.cn: 笑容可以被当作一样看得见的东西，于是动词派生出名词。

branches.en: Both the happy and the forced grin are made with effort in the muscles of the face.
branches.cn: 真笑和假笑都要动用脸上的肌肉，所以同属一组。

intro.en: Grin is a native Germanic verb with no prefix, so its family grows by English suffixes and compounds such as grinning and ear-to-ear.
intro.cn: grin 是本土的日耳曼语动词，没有前缀，它的词族靠英语后缀与复合说法扩展。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source has been established for grin, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: grin 没有可靠的拉丁语来源，所以拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Grin is the base form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: grin 是动词原形。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词或名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms grinning.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 grinning。

items.example: A grinning boy waved from the car.
items.exampleCN: 一个咧嘴笑的小男孩从车里招手。

items.example: A double n marks the past tense: grinned.
items.exampleCN: 过去式要把 n 双写：grinned。

items.meaningCN: 表示「做某动作的人」的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er brings out grinner.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 可以构成 grinner。

items.example: The suffix -ly gives grinningly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 可以构成 grinningly。

items.example: There was nothing to do but grin and bear it.
items.exampleCN: 除了咬牙忍着，别无办法。

items.example: They were grinning ear-to-ear after the win.
items.exampleCN: 赢了之后他们笑得合不拢嘴。

items.example: Grind differs from grin by a single letter.
items.exampleCN: grind 与 grin 只差一个字母。

definition_zh: 呻吟；哼哼；抱怨；发吱嘎声；呻吟声
definition_en: to make a long low sound that shows pain, sadness, or effort, or to complain loudly; also such a sound, or the creaking noise of wood or machinery
core_image: 躺在地上的伤员紧闭双眼，喉咙里拖出一声低沉的长叹
scene: 搬运工把最后一箱货抬上台阶，忍不住从喉咙深处发出一声长长的呻吟。The porter set down the last box and let out a long groan of exhaustion.
sceneCN: 这里 groan 是「呻吟、哼声」（第 1 个义项：因疼痛、疲倦或不满而发出低沉的长声）；句意：搬运工放下最后一只箱子，疲惫地长长呻吟了一声。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，指爱哼唧抱怨的人，也可指让人呻吟的沉重事物
由 groaning 加 -ly 构成，义为「呻吟着地」「吱嘎作响地」

senses.title: A long low sound of pain
senses.definition: to make a long low sound that shows pain, tiredness, or sadness
senses.definitionCN: 因疼痛、疲倦或悲伤而发出低沉而拖长的声音
senses.example: The injured man groaned as he tried to sit up.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤的男人试着坐起来时呻吟起来。
senses.why: The Old English verb granian already meant to moan, so the first sense is the raw human sound kept from the earliest stage of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的 granian 本就表示呻吟，所以第一义项是这个词最早阶段就保留下来的本能声音。

senses.title: To complain about something
senses.definition: to complain loudly or unhappily about something you must do
senses.definitionCN: 对不得不做的事大声或不满地抱怨
senses.example: Students groan every time the teacher mentions a test.
senses.exampleCN: 每次老师提到考试，学生们就一片抱怨声。
senses.why: A disappointed group echoes the same low sound, so the physical moan drifts into the social act of complaining.
senses.whyCN: 一群人失望时会发出同一种低迷的声音，于是身体的呻吟延伸成了社交性的抱怨。

senses.title: A creaking sound
senses.definition: to make a low creaking or grinding noise when carrying a heavy load
senses.definitionCN: 承受重压时发出低沉的吱嘎或摩擦声
senses.example: The old wooden stairs groaned under our weight.
senses.exampleCN: 老旧的木楼梯在我们脚下吱嘎作响。
senses.why: Physical moaning passes to objects that seem to suffer under a load, so wood and metal are said to groan.
senses.whyCN: 身体受压时发出的呻吟转移到承重之物上，于是木头与金属也被说成在呻吟。

senses.title: A groan as a noun
senses.definition: a long low sound made by a person, animal, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物、物体发出的低沉长声
senses.example: A groan went round the room when the match was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛取消时，屋里响起一片不满的哼哼声。
senses.why: English freely turns verbs into matching nouns, so the act of groaning becomes the countable sound itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用动词零派生名词，于是「呻吟」这个动作变成了可数的声音本身。

senses.title: To say something with a groan
senses.definition: to speak words in a low unhappy voice that shows pain or reluctance
senses.definitionCN: 用低沉、不快、显出痛苦或勉强的声音说出话来
senses.example: I will do it, he groaned, and reached for his coat.
senses.exampleCN: 「我去吧，」他哼哼着说，伸手去拿外套。
senses.why: Once groaning is a sound, it can carry speech, so the verb takes an object and means to utter it in that voice.
senses.whyCN: 呻吟一旦被当作一种声音，就能承载话语，于是动词可以带宾语，表示用那种声音说出来。

senses.title: To be weighed down by trouble
senses.definition: to be burdened by too much of something and show it
senses.definitionCN: 因某物过多而承受重压并显露出来
senses.example: The hospital system is groaning under the strain.
senses.exampleCN: 医院系统在重压之下不堪重负。
senses.why: From creaking furniture the image spreads to institutions, which seem to complain aloud as they carry excess weight.
senses.whyCN: 从吱嘎作响的家具出发，这一意象扩散到机构身上，仿佛它们扛着过量的负担而呻唤。

senses.title: Something useful but very hard to bear
senses.definition: a long, dull, and painful task that people dread
senses.definitionCN: 冗长乏味、令人害怕的苦差事
senses.example: Learning irregular verbs is a real groan for most learners.
senses.exampleCN: 学不规则动词对大多数学习者来说是件叫人头疼的苦差事。
senses.why: Anything that makes people groan gets called a groan, so the sound names the task that provokes it.
senses.whyCN: 任何让人呻吟的事物都会被叫成「一声呻吟」，于是这种声音转指引发它的任务。

intro.en: Groan is a native English word, from Old English granian, to moan; it is probably imitative, but its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: groan 是英语本土词，来自古英语 granian（呻吟）；一般认为带模仿声音的特点，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: A reconstructed form graino is thought to lie behind the word; its deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为背后有重构形式 graino（前加星号），更早的词根来源不确定。

items.en: Granian means to moan or lament in pain.
items.cn: 古英语 granian 表示因痛苦而呻吟、哀叹。

items.en: The form shifts towards gronen and the word is used of beasts and of whining protests.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐演变为 gronen，开始用于动物，也带上了嘟囔抱怨的意味。

items.en: Groan is extended to things that creak under a heavy load.
items.cn: groan 被推广到承重时吱嘎作响的物体。

items.en: Modern English freely uses the word for loud complaints and for overburdened systems.
items.cn: 现代英语把该词自由地用于大声抱怨以及不堪重负的系统。

note.en: Groan belongs to a small sound family with moan, grumble, and remember, plus the unrelated look-alike groan and grunt pair of noisy words.
note.cn: groan 与 moan、grumble、remember 同属表示声音与哼声的小家族，还要与拼写相近、词源无关的噪音词区分。

entries.definition: to make a low sound of pain or misery
entries.definitionCN: 与 groan 只差首字母，意思几乎相同；词源不同，只是读音相近

entries.definition: to make a short low sound like a pig
entries.definitionCN: 短而低的咕哝声，比 groan 更短促；与 groan 只是拼写和读音相近

entries.definition: to make a deep angry sound like an angry dog
entries.definitionCN: 低沉的咆哮，多含威胁之意；与 groan 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to breathe out slowly to show sadness or relief
entries.definitionCN: 叹气；多为短而轻的呼气，groan 更低沉、更持续

entries.definition: to cry with a long high sound
entries.definitionCN: 哀号；音调高而长，groan 则低沉闷在喉咙里

entries.definition: to complain in a low unhappy voice
entries.definitionCN: 低声嘟囔抱怨，偏向话语；groan 偏向声音本身

normalIntro.en: Groan is the first sound out of a body that hurts, and English stretched it from people to stairs, books, and institutions.
normalIntro.cn: groan 是身体受伤时最先发出的声音，英语把它从人扩展到了楼梯、书本和机构身上。

normal.en: Groan starts with the same consonant pair as grumble and grip, all deep in the throat.
normal.cn: groan 与 grumble、grip 共享沉闷的舌尖后塞音开头，声音都压在喉咙里。

normal.en: The pair groan and moan differ only in the first letter and mean almost the same thing.
normal.cn: groan 与 moan 只差首字母，意思几乎一样，可成对记背。

normal.en: Fixed phrases help: let out a groan, groan with pain, groan in despair.
normal.cn: 记住固定搭配：let out a groan、groan with pain、groan in despair。

normal.en: The past tense is groaned, adding -ed to the base without any doubling.
normal.cn: 过去式是 groaned，直接在词尾加 -ed，词尾不双写。

normal.en: Compare moan: it is softer and sadder, while groan is louder and more tied to effort and pain.
normal.cn: 对比 moan：它更轻更哀伤，groan 更响，更贴近用力和疼痛。

abstract.en: Picture a patient on a hospital bed biting the pillow and letting a low hum escape.
abstract.cn: 想象病人躺在病床上咬着枕头，让一声低沉的哼声从嘴边漏出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole classroom sighing as one when the teacher hands out a surprise quiz.
abstract.cn: 想象老师突然宣布小测，整个教室同时响起一片哼声。

abstract.en: See a heavy wardrobe pressing on a floorboard until the wood complains.
abstract.cn: 看见沉重的衣柜压在地板上，木板终于发出抱怨般的声音。

examples.en: She groaned with pain as the doctor pressed her ankle.
examples.cn: 医生按她的脚踝时，她痛得呻吟起来。

examples.en: The crowd groaned when the referee blew the whistle.
examples.cn: 裁判吹哨时，人群发出一片不满的哼声。

examples.en: We heard a low groan from the other side of the door.
examples.cn: 我们听见门那头传来一声低沉的呻吟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「咕噜嗯」——喉咙里滚出一串低低的咕噜声，就是呻吟；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 granian（呻吟、哀叹）→ 中古英语 gronen → 早期现代英语 groan；重构的古日耳曼语形式约为 graino，更早来源不确定，一般认为带拟声特点，核心义「低沉拖长的痛苦之声」。

sensesIntro.en: Groan starts as a bodily sound of pain, extends to complaint, moves onto creaking objects, and finally covers systems that are overloaded.
sensesIntro.cn: groan 从身体疼痛之声出发，转向抱怨，再转移到吱嘎作响的物体，最后指不堪重负的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low long sound escaping from a body in pain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声低沉的长音从疼痛的身体里漏出来。

branches.en: The physical sound of pain is the root sense.
branches.cn: 身体疼痛时发出的声音是根源义项。

branches.en: A group complaint echoes the same low sound socially.
branches.cn: 群体的抱怨在社会层面回响出同一种低音。

branches.en: Objects under weight borrow the sound of a body being crushed.
branches.cn: 承重之物借用了身体受压迫时的声音。

branches.en: The verb can become a noun, or carry speech in a groaning voice.
branches.cn: 动词可转化为名词，也可以带宾语表示用呻吟的语调说话。

branches.en: Institutions and dull tasks both make people or systems groan.
branches.cn: 机构与人所厌恶的苦差事都会让人或系统呻吟。

intro.en: Groan is a Germanic root word that takes no real prefix, but English builds groaner, groaning, and the zero noun groan around it.
intro.cn: groan 是日耳曼语系的根词，没有真正的前缀，英语围绕它构成 groaner、groaning 和零派生名词 groan。

latinIntro.en: Groan has no reliable Latin relative; the nearest cousins are Germanic words for crying and groaning.
latinIntro.cn: groan 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，最近的亲属是各日耳曼语中表示哭喊与呻吟的词。

items.example: The Old English verb granian is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 古英语动词 granian 是直接来源。

items.meaning: to make a low sound of pain
items.example: Groan is the everyday core verb.
items.exampleCN: groan 是日常核心动词。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er turns groan into groaner.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 groan 变成 groaner。

items.example: A groaner complains all day long.
items.exampleCN: groaner 整天抱怨不停。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms groaning.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 groaning。

items.meaning: making a groan; the sound itself
items.example: Groaning describes an ongoing low sound.
items.exampleCN: groaning 描述持续不断的低音。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms groaningly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 groaningly。

items.meaning: to make a low sound of pain
items.example: Moan is the closest everyday partner.
items.exampleCN: moan 是最近似的日常伙伴词。

items.meaning: to complain in a low voice
items.example: Grumble carries the quieter complaint.
items.exampleCN: grumble 承担更轻的抱怨义。

definition_zh: 摸索；暗中摸；探索；摸索着前行；抚摸
definition_en: to search for something by feeling with your hands, especially in the dark, or to try to find an answer by uncertain effort
core_image: 黑暗中伸出双手，掌心张开，在看不见的空气里一寸一寸地摸索
scene: 停电后，她沿着墙壁摸索着去找蜡烛。When the lights went out, she had to grope along the wall for a candle.
sceneCN: 这里 grope 是「摸索」（第 1 个义项：在看不见的地方用手摸索）；句意：灯一灭，她只好沿着墙壁摸索着去找蜡烛。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词形容词化，义为「摸索的」「心中含混不确定的」
由动词加 -er 构成，指摸索的人，也可指随意触摸他人身体者
由 groping 加 -ly 构成，义为「摸索地」「不知所措地」

senses.title: To feel around for something
senses.definition: to search for something by moving your hands about, usually when you cannot see
senses.definitionCN: 在看不见的情况下用手四处移动来寻找某物
senses.example: He groped for his glasses on the bedside table.
senses.exampleCN: 他在床头柜上摸索着找眼镜。
senses.why: The Germanic root meant to seize with the hand, so the first sense is the hand working without the help of sight.
senses.whyCN: 古日耳曼词根意为用手抓握，所以第一义项就是手在失去视觉帮助时的动作。

senses.title: To move blindly forward
senses.definition: to move slowly and with difficulty because you cannot see the way
senses.definitionCN: 因看不清道路而缓慢艰难地移动
senses.example: Rescue workers groped through the smoke towards the exit.
senses.exampleCN: 救援人员穿过浓烟摸索着朝出口走去。
senses.why: Searching with the hands becomes searching for a path, so the verb also describes an unseeing journey.
senses.whyCN: 用手寻找物体会变成寻找道路，所以该动词也描述一段看不见的行程。

senses.title: To search mentally for an idea
senses.definition: to try to find a word, answer, or idea without being sure where it is
senses.definitionCN: 不确定答案在哪里，却仍努力去找词语、答案或想法
senses.example: She groped for the right word in French.
senses.exampleCN: 她搜肠刮肚地找那个恰当的法语词。
senses.why: The hands of the mind reach into the dark just as the real hands do, so groping becomes an image for uncertain thinking.
senses.whyCN: 心灵之手和真实的手一样会伸进黑暗，于是摸索成了不确定思考的比喻。

senses.title: To seek a solution over time
senses.definition: to work towards a plan or answer by trial rather than clear knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 不依靠清晰认识，而靠不断尝试去接近方案或答案
senses.example: The new team groped towards a workable policy.
senses.exampleCN: 新团队一步步摸索出一套可行的政策。
senses.why: A long blind walk mirrors a long period of trial, so the verb covers slow institutional search as well.
senses.whyCN: 一段漫长的盲行就如同一段漫长的试探，所以该词也能覆盖缓慢的制度性探索。

senses.title: To touch a person improperly
senses.definition: to touch someone in a sexual way without being invited
senses.definitionCN: 未经同意以色情或越界的方式触摸他人
senses.example: A passenger claimed the man had groped her on the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 一名乘客称那名男子在公交车上对她乱摸。
senses.why: Hands that search for a knob can also search over a body, and that literal moving of hands hardened into the unwanted-touch sense.
senses.whyCN: 寻找开关的手也可能在他人身上游移，这种字面上的摸索逐渐固化为不受欢迎的触摸义。

senses.title: A blind attempt in the dark
senses.definition: an attempt made without sight or clear information, often used in the phrase a blind grope
senses.definitionCN: 在看不见或信息不明时的一次尝试，多见于口头短语
senses.example: Finding the file was a blind grope until we checked the index.
senses.exampleCN: 在查过索引之前，找那份文件完全是盲人摸象。
senses.why: The old noun counterpart of the verb survives in set phrases, where groping names a single blind effort.
senses.whyCN: 该动词古老的名词对应形式保留在固定短语里，表示一次盲目的努力。

intro.en: Grope comes from Old English grapian, to feel with the hands, which is related to gripan, to grip; the deeper root is uncertain.
intro.cn: grope 来自古英语 grapian（用手摸索），与 gripan（抓握）同源；更早的词根来源不确定。

items.en: A reconstructed root graip- links hands that reach out and hands that seize; its Sanskrit and Greek links are debated.
items.cn: 一般认为有重构词根 graip-，把手伸出去与手抓握住连在一起；与梵语、希腊语的关系尚有争议。

items.en: Grapian means to feel or take hold of something with the hands.
items.cn: 古英语 grapian 表示用手触摸或抓住某物。

items.en: The Germanic p becomes a b in modern spelling, giving grope, and the word is used of blind walking.
items.cn: 在现代拼写中，日耳曼语的 p 变成 b，于是写作 grope，并开始用于黑暗中行走。

items.en: Grope is applied to the mind as well, as in groping for words.
items.cn: grope 也被用于心智活动，如 groping for words（搜词）。

items.en: The verb takes on figurative uses for uncertain policies and a separate sense of unwanted touching.
items.cn: 这个动词产生了指不确定政策的比喻用法，以及独立的「不正当触摸」义。

note.en: Grope is knit into the family of gripan and grasp, and sits beside search words that describe hands feeling their way.
note.cn: grope 属于 gripan、grasp 一族的词，与描写手探路的「查找」类动词相邻。

entries.definition: to take hold of something firmly
entries.definitionCN: 紧握；与 grope 同源，但义为牢牢抓住而非摸索

entries.definition: to grip tightly, or to complain
entries.definitionCN: 紧握或抱怨；与 grope 共享抓握词根

entries.definition: to seize something quickly
entries.definitionCN: 迅速抓住；与本词族相关，但只是拼写相近、动作更快

entries.definition: to move the hands clumsily while searching
entries.definitionCN: 笨拙地摸索；grope 重在探路，fumble 重在手脚不灵

entries.definition: to touch something to find out what it is
entries.definitionCN: 触摸感知；最基础的手部动作，grope 带盲目和费力

entries.definition: to search wildly with the hands
entries.definitionCN: 乱抓乱扒地找；比 grope 更慌乱

normalIntro.en: Grope keeps the old Germanic hand in it: the same grab and grip family, only now the hand works in the dark.
normalIntro.cn: grope 保留着古老日耳曼语的手部意象：和 grab、grip 同出一族，只是如今这只手在黑暗里工作。

normal.en: Grope sits in the same word family as grasp, grip, and grab, all about hands.
normal.cn: grope 与 grasp、grip、grab 同属手部动作词族。

normal.en: The letter p in grope points at the older form grapian, where groping first began.
normal.cn: grope 里的字母 p 提示了更早的形式 grapian，摸索义最早从那里开始。

normal.en: Remember the phrases grope for the light switch and grope around in the dark.
normal.cn: 记住搭配 grope for the light switch 和 grope around in the dark。

normal.en: Grope doubles no consonant before -ing and -ed: groping, groped.
normal.cn: grope 在加 -ing 和 -ed 时不双写辅音：groping、groped。

normal.en: Compare grasp: grasp is a firm hold, grope is an open searching hand.
normal.cn: 对比 grasp：grasp 是牢牢握住，grope 是张开手四处搜寻。

abstract.en: Picture two hands stretched forward in a dark hallway, palms down, moving slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象在黑暗的走廊里伸出两只手，掌心向下，慢慢移动。

abstract.en: See a hiker feeling the stone wall for a handhold in thick fog.
abstract.cn: 看见徒步者在浓雾中摸索石墙，想找一处可以抓握的地方。

abstract.en: Imagine a mind reaching for a forgotten name, touching letters it cannot quite hold.
abstract.cn: 想象头脑去够一个忘掉的名字，碰到几个字母却抓不牢。

examples.en: She groped in her bag for the keys.
examples.cn: 她在包里摸索着找钥匙。

examples.en: The hikers groped their way down the mountain in the fog.
examples.cn: 徒步者在雾中摸索着下山。

examples.en: He groped for an explanation but found none.
examples.cn: 他努力想找个解释，却一个也找不到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「狗肉铺」——黑灯瞎火在铺子里找东西，只能伸手到处摸索；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 grapian（用手摸、抓）← 古日耳曼语重构词根 graip-（伸手抓握）→ 与 gripan（抓握，即今 grip）同族 → 中古英语 grope；核心义「手在黑暗中摸索」。

sensesIntro.en: Grope begins with hands searching in the dark, extends to walking blind, then to thinking without clear answers, and finally to a separate sense of improper touching.
sensesIntro.cn: grope 从黑暗中用手摸索开始，扩展到盲行、没有把握的思考，最后发展出不正当触摸的独立义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open hands feeling through the dark for something unseen.
core.cn: 核心意象：张开双手在黑暗里摸索看不见的东西。

branches.en: Hands search for an object the eyes cannot find.
branches.cn: 肉眼找不到的物体，由手指去寻找。

branches.en: The searching hands become the whole body finding a way.
branches.cn: 摸索的双手扩展成整个身体寻找道路。

branches.en: The mind borrows the same blind reach when word hunting.
branches.cn: 心中找词时，借用了同样的盲手探路。

branches.en: A long process of trial and a single blind attempt both keep the dark in view.
branches.cn: 长期的试探与单次的盲试都保留着黑暗这一元素。

branches.en: Hands moving across a body turn the search into an unwanted touch.
branches.cn: 手在他人身上游移，使寻找变成了不受欢迎的触摸。

intro.en: Grope is a Germanic base verb with no Latin parts; English builds groping, groper, and gropingly from it by ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: grope 是没有拉丁成分的日耳曼语根词，英语用普通后缀围绕它构成 groping、groper 和 gropingly。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin ancestor of grope; its relatives are Germanic hand words such as grip and grasp.
latinIntro.cn: grope 没有可靠的拉丁语祖形，它的亲属是 grip、grasp 等日耳曼语手部词。

items.example: Old English grapian supplies the first image.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 grapian 提供了最初的意象。

items.example: Grope is the modern core form.
items.exampleCN: grope 是现代核心形式。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms groping.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 groping。

items.example: Groping is both a participle and a noun.
items.exampleCN: groping 既是分词也是名词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms groper.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 groper。

items.example: A groper searches with the hands.
items.exampleCN: groper 是用手摸索的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms gropingly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 gropingly。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms groped.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 groped。

items.example: Gripan is a close cousin of grapian.
items.exampleCN: gripan 是 grapian 的近亲。

definition_zh: 严重地；极其；过分地；粗鲁地；粗俗地
definition_en: in a very great or serious degree; also in a coarse or disgusting way
core_image: 天平一端堆满砝码，指针被压得严重歪向一边
scene: 审计报告指出，这家公司的广告费用被严重夸大了。The audit found that the company had grossly exaggerated its advertising costs.
sceneCN: 这里 grossly 是「严重地、极大地」（第 1 个义项：程度远超正常范围）；句意：审计发现这家公司严重夸大了广告费用。

derivatives.zh: 副词 grossly 的形容词原形，义为「总的」「严重的」「粗俗的」
由 gross 加 -ness 构成，义为「粗俗」「严重程度」
同形动词，常用作 gross up，义为「使（金额）增至总额」

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: to a degree that is very great and clearly beyond what is normal or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 达到极大且明显超出正常或可接受范围的程度
senses.example: The figures were grossly exaggerated in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里的数字被严重夸大了。
senses.why: The adjective gross meant large or thick in old French, so the adverb naturally means to a very large degree.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 gross 在古法语中意为「大、厚」，因此副词自然表示「达到很大程度」。

senses.title: In a shocking or wrong way
senses.definition: in a way that is so clearly wrong that it shocks people
senses.definitionCN: 错得如此明显，以致令人震惊
senses.example: The hospital was grossly negligent in its record keeping.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院在病历管理上严重失职。
senses.why: Beyond normal size lies beyond normal conduct, so grossly comes to mark failures serious enough to be scandalous.
senses.whyCN: 超出正常的尺度就超出了正常的行为，于是 grossly 用来标记严重到令人哗然的失误。

senses.title: In a coarse manner
senses.definition: in a rough, vulgar, or disgusting way
senses.definitionCN: 以粗糙、粗俗或令人厌恶的方式
senses.example: He spoke grossly of his colleagues at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 他在餐桌上粗鲁地议论同事。
senses.why: Latin grossus means thick or coarse, and the thick body image hardened into the sense of crude personal behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 grossus 意为粗厚，粗厚的身体意象逐渐固化为举止粗俗的含义。

senses.title: Applied to amounts and payments
senses.definition: in relation to the whole amount before tax or other deductions
senses.definitionCN: 就税或其他扣除之前的全部金额而言
senses.example: The consultants were grossly overpaid for six weeks of work.
senses.exampleCN: 顾问们为六周的工作拿到了过高的毛报酬。
senses.why: The commerce sense of gross, the whole amount, joins the adverb, and with adjectives like paid it signals excessive total payment.
senses.whyCN: 商业义中 gross 指全部金额，与副词结合后再接 paid 这类词，表示总额过高。

senses.title: To a displeasing extent
senses.definition: to a degree that arouses strong disapproval or disgust
senses.definitionCN: 达到引起强烈不满或厌恶的程度
senses.example: The party was grossly extravagant at a time of cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 在削减开支的时期，这场宴会铺张得令人反感。
senses.why: The coarse and the excessive senses merge, so grossly can describe excess that also feels in bad taste.
senses.whyCN: 「粗俗」与「过度」两个方向合流，于是 grossly 可以形容既逾矩又俗气的铺张。

intro.en: Grossly comes from gross, which entered English through Old French gros from Late Latin grossus, thick or large, of uncertain origin; the English -ly is native.
intro.cn: grossly 来自 gross，后者经古法语 gros 进入英语，源头是晚期拉丁语 grossus（粗厚、大），更早来源不确定；英语词尾 -ly 则是本土成分。

items.en: Late Latin grossus means thick or coarse; its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 grossus 意为粗、厚；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Gros means large, fat, or thick and gives English its basic meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 gros 意为大、肥、厚，为英语提供了基本含义。

items.en: Gross enters English for large or coarse things.
items.cn: gross 进入英语，表示大的或粗糙的事物。

items.en: A trade sense of the whole number of twelve, a dozen, grows, and gross comes to describe total amounts.
items.cn: 一个计十二个的整数的商业义出现，gross 开始用来描述总额。

items.en: Grossly settles into the adverbial senses of extreme degree and coarse behaviour.
items.cn: grossly 定型为表示极端程度与粗俗行为的副词义项。

note.en: Grossly is built on gross and shares its family of grossness and gross, while sitting near adverbs of degree such as utterly and badly.
note.cn: grossly 由 gross 派生，与 grossness 和 gross 同族，又靠近 utterly、badly 这类程度副词。

entries.definition: total, extreme, or coarse
entries.definitionCN: 总的；严重的；粗俗的；grossly 的形容词原形

entries.definition: the quality of being coarse or extreme
entries.definitionCN: 粗俗；严重程度；由 gross 加名词后缀构成

entries.definition: more gross; also a person who earns a gross sum
entries.definitionCN: 更粗俗的；也可指赚取毛收入的人；与 grossly 拼写相近

entries.definition: completely
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；语气最重，常与否定或错误表示搭配

entries.definition: to a serious degree
entries.definitionCN: 严重地；较口语，grossly 更正式

entries.definition: to too great a degree
entries.definitionCN: 过度地；强调超出限度，未必带道德评判

normalIntro.en: Grossly is simply gross plus the native -ly, and gross itself goes back to thick and large, so the adverb pushes any quality to a wrong extreme.
normalIntro.cn: grossly 就是 gross 加本土词尾 -ly；gross 本义「粗、厚、大」，所以这个副词把任何品质推向错误的极端。

normal.en: The -ly ending marks an adverb, so grossly describes how serious or how coarse something is.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 表明它是副词，所以 grossly 说明某事严重或粗俗到什么程度。

normal.en: Grossly usually joins a strong adjective: grossly unfair, grossly inadequate, grossly negligent.
normal.cn: grossly 常接语气很强的形容词：grossly unfair、grossly inadequate、grossly negligent。

normal.en: Gross and grossly keep the Latin grossus sense of thick, which links excess with coarseness.
normal.cn: gross 与 grossly 保留拉丁语 grossus 的「粗厚」义，由此把过度与粗俗连在一起。

normal.en: In business, gross means before deductions, hence grossly paid and gross income.
normal.cn: 在商业里 gross 表示扣除之前，所以有 grossly paid 和 gross income。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with greatly: greatly praises a size, grossly condemns it.
normal.cn: 别把它和 greatly 搞混：greatly 中性甚至赞扬程度，grossly 带着批评。

abstract.en: Picture a balance scale with one pan loaded far too full, hanging at a steep angle.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一边堆得过满，已歪成很陡的角度。

abstract.en: Imagine a red stamp reading error on a hospital file that no one checked.
abstract.cn: 想象一份无人核对的病历上盖着醒目的「严重失误」红章。

abstract.en: See a thick, rough rope held by a voice that talks in the same rough way.
abstract.cn: 看见一根粗糙的绳子，而说话的声音也像它一样粗糙。

examples.en: The report grossly overstated the risks of the treatment.
examples.cn: 那份报告严重高估了这种疗法的风险。

examples.en: It would be grossly unfair to blame one student for the failure.
examples.cn: 把失败归咎于一个学生将是极不公平的。

examples.en: The company was grossly overpaid for work it never completed.
examples.cn: 这家公司从未完成工作，却拿到了过高的报酬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「够死哩」——天平的一端「够死」地往下沉，那份量严重得离谱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 晚期拉丁语 grossus（粗、厚；来源不确定）→ 古法语 gros（大、肥、厚）→ 中古英语 gross（大的、粗糙的）→ gross + 本土副词词尾 -ly → grossly，核心义「在程度上粗重地超出」。

sensesIntro.en: Grossly keeps the thick, large core of gross and spreads it into extreme degree, serious wrongdoing, coarse behaviour, gross amounts, and offensive excess.
sensesIntro.cn: grossly 保留了 gross「粗厚、大」的核心，并扩展为极端程度、严重过失、粗俗举止、毛额与令人反感的铺张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale loaded far past balance on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一端堆载过多，远远失去平衡。

branches.en: The large core becomes the plain sense of extreme degree.
branches.cn: 「大」的核心转化为纯粹的极端程度义。

branches.en: Extreme size turns into wrongdoing big enough to shock.
branches.cn: 过大的尺寸转为大到令人震惊的过错。

branches.en: The thick body in Latin survives as the sense of coarse behaviour.
branches.cn: 拉丁语中「粗厚」的实体延续为粗俗举止之义。

branches.en: The trade sense of the whole amount yields the money use.
branches.cn: 商业上「全部金额」的义项带来了金钱用法。

branches.en: Excess plus coarseness together produce a sense of offensive overdoing.
branches.cn: 过度与粗俗叠加，产生令人反感的过分铺张感。

intro.en: Grossly is a transparent compound: the loan word gross plus the native adverb suffix -ly, with grossness as its noun partner.
intro.cn: grossly 结构透明：外来词 gross 加上本土副词词尾 -ly，名词形式为 grossness。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is grossus, thick or coarse, which also gives French gros and English grocer through the selling of goods in bulk.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 grossus（粗、厚），它也通过「大宗售卖货物」这条线产生了法语 gros 和英语 grocer。

items.example: Late Latin grossus gives the thick core.
items.exampleCN: 晚期拉丁语 grossus 提供「粗厚」的核心。

items.example: Old French gros carries the word to England.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 gros 把这个词带到英格兰。

items.example: Gross keeps both the size and the coarse senses.
items.exampleCN: gross 同时保留「尺度」与「粗俗」两类义。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns gross into grossly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 gross 变成 grossly。

items.meaning: to an extreme or coarse degree
items.example: Grossly modifies strong judgements.
items.exampleCN: grossly 修饰语气强烈的判断。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms grossness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 grossness。

items.example: Grossness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: grossness 表示这种性质本身。

items.meaning: a dealer in food sold in bulk
items.example: Grocer came from selling goods by the gross.
items.exampleCN: grocer 来自按整批出售货物的说法。

items.example: The suffix -er serves as in grocer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 在 grocer 中发挥作用。

definition_zh: 脾气坏的；爱发牢骚的；闷闷不乐的
definition_en: bad-tempered and irritable, often for no clear reason
core_image: 清早没睡够的人沉着脸，谁搭话都嫌烦
scene: 他整晚没睡好，早饭时谁跟他说话都被顶了回去。He was so grouchy that morning that every cheerful remark annoyed him.
sceneCN: 这里 grouchy 是「脾气坏、爱发牢骚」（第 1 个义项：因烦躁而脾气坏）；句意：那天早上他脾气坏透了，每一句好话都让他恼火。

pos.zh: 脾气坏的；爱发牢骚的；闷闷不乐的

derivatives.zh: 基础词派生：由形容词 grouchy 去词尾 -y 得到，义为「发牢骚；抱怨」
由形容词转成的名词，义为「爱抱怨的人；牢骚」
基础词加副词词尾 -ly，义为「脾气坏地；嘟囔着」
基础词加名词词尾 -ness，义为「坏脾气；牢骚气」

senses.title: Bad-tempered and easily annoyed
senses.definition: irritable and easily annoyed, especially over small things
senses.definitionCN: 烦躁易怒，尤其对小事也容易发火
senses.example: He gets grouchy when he has not slept well.
senses.exampleCN: 他没睡好时脾气就变坏。
senses.why: The word grew from grouch, a person who grumbles; the grim look comes first, then the short temper.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 grouch（爱嘟囔抱怨的人）长出来：先有那张阴沉的脸，再有坏脾气。

senses.title: Grumbling and complaining
senses.definition: often complaining in a low, cross voice
senses.definitionCN: 常低声抱怨、嘟囔不满
senses.example: The grouchy neighbour grumbled about the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 那位爱抱怨的邻居絮叨起噪音来。
senses.why: A person who grumbles all day sounds grouchy, so the complaining habit becomes part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 一个人整天嘟囔抱怨，听起来就 grouchy，于是「抱怨的习惯」也进入词义。

senses.title: Sullen in mood
senses.definition: sulky and silent with a sour mood
senses.definitionCN: 闷着脸、沉默而不高兴
senses.example: She sat grouchy in the corner after losing the game.
senses.exampleCN: 输了比赛后，她闷闷不乐地坐在角落里。
senses.why: The sour face shows mood without words, so grouchy also names the silent sulk.
senses.whyCN: 阴沉的脸不说话也能表达情绪，所以 grouchy 也指闷声不乐的样子。

senses.title: Describing a gloomy period
senses.titleCN: 指气氛沉闷的一段时间
senses.definition: used of a period or place that feels dull and bad-humoured
senses.definitionCN: 形容一段时间或一处地方沉闷、气氛不好
senses.example: It was a grouchy week of rain and delays.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个阴雨连绵、事事拖延的烦躁星期。
senses.why: Once the word describes a person, it stretches to a time or place where everyone feels cross.
senses.whyCN: 词义从人扩展到时间段或场所：所有人都烦躁，那段时间就成了 grouchy 的一周。

intro.en: Grouchy is an English adjective built on grouch, a word of uncertain origin meaning to grumble or be bad-tempered.
intro.cn: grouchy 是英语在 grouch 基础上构成的形容词；grouch 意为嘟囔、闹脾气，其来源不确定。

items.en: Grouch has no settled source; some link it to grutch, an older form meaning to grumble.
items.cn: grouch 的来源没有定论；一般认为它与古形式 grutch（嘟囔、抱怨）有关。

items.en: Grutch and grouche appear in English meaning to complain.
items.cn: 中古英语时期出现 grutch、grouche 等形式，意为抱怨。

items.en: Grouch names a person who complains all the time.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪用 grouch 指总是抱怨的人。

items.en: The adjective grouchy is formed with the common ending -y.
items.cn: 形容词 grouchy 由常见词尾 -y 构成。

items.en: Grouchy spreads in informal American speech as a word for a cross mood.
items.cn: grouchy 在美式口语中流行开来，用来形容坏情绪。

items.en: Today grouchy describes a mild, passing bad temper.
items.cn: 如今 grouchy 多形容轻微、一时的坏脾气。

note.en: Grouchy is a mild bad-temper word, near grouch and grouchiness, and close to grumpy, irritable, and cranky.
note.cn: grouchy 表示轻微坏脾气，与 grouch、grouchiness 同族，与 grumpy、irritable、cranky 意思相近。

entries.definition: to grumble or complain
entries.definitionCN: 嘟囔；抱怨

entries.definition: in a bad-tempered way
entries.definitionCN: 脾气坏地；嘟囔着

entries.definition: a bad-tempered mood
entries.definitionCN: 坏脾气；牢骚气

entries.definition: bad-tempered and easily annoyed
entries.definitionCN: 脾气坏的；爱生气的

entries.definition: easily made angry
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的；急躁的

entries.definition: in a bad mood and complaining
entries.definitionCN: 闹情绪的；爱抱怨的

normalIntro.en: Grouchy is grouch plus -y, which turns a grumbling person into a grumbling mood.
normalIntro.cn: grouchy 是 grouch 加 -y：把「爱嘟囔的人」变成「爱嘟囔的脾气」。

normal.en: Grouch is the base word for a person who complains.
normal.cn: grouch 是基础词，指爱抱怨的人。

normal.en: The ending -y makes adjectives from nouns, as in rain and rainy.
normal.cn: 词尾 -y 把名词变形容词，如 rain 与 rainy。

normal.en: Grouchy often follows be or get: he is grouchy today.
normal.cn: grouchy 常跟在 be 或 get 后：he is grouchy today（他今天脾气不好）。

normal.en: Compare grumpy: grumpy is a set mood, grouchy is a passing one.
normal.cn: 对比 grumpy：grumpy 偏固定的性情，grouchy 多指一时的情绪。

normal.en: The adverb is grouchily and the noun is grouchiness.
normal.cn: 副词是 grouchily，名词是 grouchiness。

abstract.en: Picture a face like a closed door before breakfast.
abstract.cn: 想象早饭前一张像关紧的门那样的脸。

abstract.en: Hear a low grumble under the breath, like an old engine.
abstract.cn: 听见压低嗓子的嘟囔声，像一台旧发动机。

abstract.en: See a child turned away in the corner, chin down.
abstract.cn: 看见一个孩子在角落里转过身，低着头。

examples.en: He was grouchy all afternoon after the long test.
examples.cn: 考完那场长考试后，他一整个下午都脾气不好。

examples.en: My grouchy uncle complains about the weather every visit.
examples.cn: 我那位爱抱怨的叔叔每次来访都要抱怨天气。

examples.en: A little sleep will cure this grouchy mood.
examples.cn: 睡一会儿就能治好这股烦躁的情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「刮臭」——脸色一沉、话里带刺，好像一路刮着臭味，谁靠近都嫌烦；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 grouch（嘟囔、闹脾气；爱抱怨的人，来源不确定，一般认为与古形式 grutch 有关）+ 形容词词尾 -y → grouchy，核心义「闹脾气的」。

sensesIntro.en: Grouchy starts from a bad-tempered mood, then adds the grumbling voice, the silent sulk, and finally a dull period.
sensesIntro.cn: grouchy 先指坏脾气，再加进嘟囔的声音、闷声不乐的样子，最后扩展到沉闷的一段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grim face before breakfast that grumbles at everyone.
core.cn: 核心意象：早饭前沉着脸，对谁都要嘟囔两句。

branches.en: The bad-temper sense is the main everyday use.
branches.cn: 坏脾气是最主要的日常义项。

branches.en: The grumbling voice is the habitual sense.
branches.cn: 嘟囔抱怨是习惯性义项。

branches.en: The silent sulk is the mood sense.
branches.cn: 闷声不乐是情绪义项。

branches.en: A cross person and a sulky person both show a sour face.
branches.cn: 脾气坏的人和闷闷不乐的人都摆出一张阴沉的脸。

branches.en: A complaining person can cast gloom over a whole week.
branches.cn: 爱抱怨的人能把一整周都搅得沉闷。

intro.en: Grouchy has a thin affix story: a base form grouch with the adjective ending -y, plus the adverb and noun endings -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: grouchy 的词缀成分不多：基础形式 grouch 加形容词词尾 -y，再加副词词尾 -ly 与名词词尾 -ness。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family behind grouchy; grouch has an uncertain source, so no Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: grouchy 背后没有拉丁词族；grouch 来源不确定，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Grouch is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: grouch 是这个形容词的基础形式。

items.example: The suffix -y turns grouch into grouchy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 grouch 变成 grouchy。

items.example: Grouchy describes a passing bad mood.
items.exampleCN: grouchy 描述一时的坏情绪。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms grouchily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 grouchily。

items.example: Grouchily tells how someone speaks.
items.exampleCN: grouchily 说明说话的方式。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms grouchiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 grouchiness。

items.example: Grouchiness names the mood itself.
items.exampleCN: grouchiness 指情绪本身。

items.example: Grouchier replaces the final y with i.
items.exampleCN: grouchier 把词尾 y 改成 i。

items.example: Grutch is a likely older relative.
items.exampleCN: grutch 可能是更早的亲属形式。

definition_zh: 小树林；果园；树丛；林荫小园
definition_en: a small wood or group of trees, or a place planted with fruit trees
core_image: 一片不太大的树林，树干成排，阳光从枝叶间漏下
scene: 那片小树林里长着老橄榄树，午后特别安静。A small grove of olive trees stood behind the farmhouse, cool and quiet in the heat.
sceneCN: 这里 grove 是「小树林」（第 1 个义项：成片生长的小树林）；句意：农舍后面有一小片橄榄树林，暑热中显得凉爽又安静。

pos.zh: 小树林；果园；树丛；林荫小园

derivatives.zh: 基础词加复数词尾 -s，义为「多片小树林」
只是拼写开头相近：来自动词 grovel（趴下、卑躬屈膝），与 grove 词源不同

senses.title: A small wood
senses.definition: a small area covered with trees, smaller than a wood or forest
senses.definitionCN: 长满树木的小片区域，比一般树林或森林小
senses.example: We picnicked in a grove of oaks.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在一片橡树林里野餐。
senses.why: The Old English word meant a small wood, and that size is still the heart of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 古英语原义就是「小树林」，「不大」这一点至今仍是词义的核心。

senses.title: A fruit-tree planting
senses.definition: an area where fruit trees such as oranges or olives are grown
senses.definitionCN: 种植柑橘、橄榄等果树的专门园地
senses.example: Her family owns an orange grove in the south.
senses.exampleCN: 她家在南方有一片橘园。
senses.why: Farmers arranged fruit trees in rows, so a grove became the usual word for a small orchard.
senses.whyCN: 果农把果树成排种下，于是 grove 成了小规模果园的常用说法。

senses.title: A group of trees in a town
senses.titleCN: 树丛；城市中的林荫小园
senses.definition: a cluster of trees planted for shade or beauty, often in a town
senses.definitionCN: 为遮阴或美观而种的树丛，常见于城镇
senses.example: A grove of maples shades the town square.
senses.exampleCN: 一片枫树林为城镇广场遮阴。
senses.why: Planted trees in a row form the same picture, so the word spreads to town settings.
senses.whyCN: 成排栽下的树构成同样的画面，所以词义延伸到城镇绿化。

senses.title: A sacred tree site
senses.definition: a small wood connected with worship or a sacred place
senses.definitionCN: 与祭祀或圣地相关的小片林地
senses.example: Ancient worshippers met in the sacred grove.
senses.exampleCN: 古代的信徒们在圣林里集会。
senses.why: In older cultures a grove was where people met the gods, so the place carried ritual meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在古老文化里，人们在树林中与神灵相会，于是这片林地带上祭祀意义。

senses.title: The name of a place group
senses.definition: used in names such as Grove Street for a tree-lined place
senses.definitionCN: 用于街道或地名，指有树的地方
senses.example: She lives on Elm Grove near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她住在车站附近的榆树巷。
senses.why: Because a grove marks a shady, planted spot, the word entered street names for such places.
senses.whyCN: 树林意味着有阴凉、有栽种，所以 grove 进入了这类地方的路名。

intro.en: Grove comes from Old English graf, a small wood, and is related to words meaning digging or cutting.
intro.cn: grove 来自古英语 graf（小树林），与表示挖掘、砍伐的词同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root graban means to dig.
items.cn: 一般认为有日耳曼语重构形式 graban，意为挖掘。

items.en: Graf means a small wood or a grove.
items.cn: 古英语 graf 意为小树林、树丛。

items.en: The spelling shifts toward grove while the meaning stays.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写逐渐变为 grove，词义不变。

items.en: Grove is used for orchards and planted fruit trees.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪前后开始用 grove 指果园和成片果树。

items.en: Grove appears regularly in street and place names.
items.cn: 现代英语中 grove 常见于街道名和地名。

note.en: Grove is a small-wood word, related to engrave and grave through digging, and close to copse, orchard, and thicket.
note.cn: grove 属于「小树林」类词，通过「挖掘」与 engrave、grave 同源，近义词有 copse、orchard、thicket。

entries.definition: to cut words or designs into a surface
entries.definitionCN: 在表面雕刻文字或图案

entries.definition: a place where a body is buried
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓（与「挖」同源）

entries.definition: a long narrow cut in a surface
entries.definitionCN: 沟槽；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a small group of trees
entries.definitionCN: 矮林；小树丛

entries.definition: an area where fruit trees are grown
entries.definitionCN: 果园

entries.definition: a group of bushes and small trees
entries.definitionCN: 灌木丛；树丛

normalIntro.en: Grove is a small, old English wood word, kept alive today mainly by place names and fruit plantings.
normalIntro.cn: grove 是古老的英语「小树林」词，今天主要靠地名和果园延续。

normal.en: Grove is smaller than wood and much smaller than forest.
normal.cn: grove 比 wood 小得多，比 forest 小得更多。

normal.en: Fruit plantings use it freely: olive grove, orange grove.
normal.cn: 果园常用它：olive grove（橄榄园）、orange grove（橘园）。

normal.en: A grove of trees needs the preposition of.
normal.cn: a grove of trees 中必须用介词 of。

normal.en: Grove shares a digging root with grave and engrave.
normal.cn: grove 与 grave、engrave 共享「挖掘」词根。

normal.en: The plural is simply groves.
normal.cn: 复数形式就是 groves。

abstract.en: Picture cool shade under a small stand of tall trunks.
abstract.cn: 想象一片高大树干下凉爽的树荫。

abstract.en: See rows of orange trees with fruit glowing in the sun.
abstract.cn: 看见成排的橘树，果实被阳光照得发亮。

abstract.en: Think of maples planted along a town square.
abstract.cn: 想到广场边成排栽下的枫树。

examples.en: A narrow path led into a grove of tall pines.
examples.cn: 一条小路通向一片高大的松树林。

examples.en: The orange groves were heavy with fruit that year.
examples.cn: 那一年橘园里果实累累。

examples.en: A sacred grove once stood beside the temple.
examples.cn: 神庙旁曾经有一片圣林。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木污」——一小片树挤在一起，树皮上带着泥土的痕迹，像一块被树围住的「木污」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 graf（小树林）+ 与 graban（挖掘）同源 → 中古英语 grove → 英语 grove，核心义「一小片林子」。

sensesIntro.en: Grove moves from a small wood to a planted fruit garden, then to town shade trees, sacred places, and place names.
sensesIntro.cn: grove 从小树林出发，扩展到人工栽种的果园、城镇遮阴的树丛、圣地林园，最后进入地名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small stand of trunks with sun falling between the leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小片林子，阳光从枝叶间落下。

branches.en: A small wood is the original sense.
branches.cn: 小树林是原本的义项。

branches.en: A fruit planting extends the wood to farm land.
branches.cn: 果园把「林」延伸到农田。

branches.en: Town shade trees are the planted sense.
branches.cn: 城镇遮阴树是人工栽种义项。

branches.en: A small wood can be a place of worship.
branches.cn: 小树林可以是祭祀场所。

branches.en: A named tree-lined spot becomes a street label.
branches.cn: 有树的地名会变成街道名称。

intro.en: Grove is a bare Old English root: no prefix and no usable suffix, so its family comes from related verbs such as engrave.
intro.cn: grove 是一个裸露的古英语词根，没有前缀也没有可用的后缀，同族词来自 engrave 等相关动词。

latinIntro.en: Grove is Germanic, not Latin; the Latin family behind engrave is gravis, so no direct Latin cognate is listed.
latinIntro.cn: grove 属于日耳曼语而非拉丁语；engrave 背后的拉丁词是 gravis，因此不列直接拉丁同源词。

items.example: Graf is the Old English shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: graf 是该词的古英语形式。

items.example: Grove keeps the small-wood sense.
items.exampleCN: grove 保留了「小树林」含义。

items.example: The plural is groves.
items.exampleCN: 复数是 groves。

items.example: Engrave shares the digging root.
items.exampleCN: engrave 与它共享「挖」的词根。

items.example: Grave shows the digging image.
items.exampleCN: grave 保留挖掘的意象。

items.example: Graban is the reconstructed root.
items.exampleCN: graban 是重构出来的词根。

items.example: Groove looks alike but is not related.
items.exampleCN: groove 只是形近，并不同源。

items.example: Grovelled only echoes the first letters.
items.exampleCN: grovelled 只是开头字母巧合。
